title: The relationship between executive remuneration and earnings management: incorporating the disclosure quality of financial reporting judgements
summary: Abstract According to managerial power theory, executives may be biased in their financial reporting judgements (FRJs), which can lead to accounting choices that increase earnings and potentially result in abnormal (excessive) executive remuneration. Global empirical studies suggest that the pursuit of higher executive remuneration can incentivise earnings management (EM) engagement. However, previous research on the relationship between EM and executive remuneration has mainly focused on developed countries, used accrual-based EM proxies, and often included only chief executive officer remuneration. The main objective of the study was to investigate the relationship between EM and executive remuneration in South Africa, a developing country, using the disclosure quality of FRJs as a measure of EM. Another unique contribution entails a more comprehensive measure of executive remuneration, covering all executive directors, and an indicator of whether the remuneration was deemed abnormal. Understanding this relationship in South Africa is vital, given the existing high levels of income inequality, particularly from a social justice perspective. Using a quantitative approach, the research examined 101 Johannesburg Stock Exchange-listed companies from 2020 to 2023. Applying regression analysis, the study found that executives may indeed be biased in their FRJs, leading to abnormal executive remuneration. The findings highlight the need for ongoing monitoring of remuneration and the quality of FRJ disclosures to mitigate the risk of rent extraction and to curb executives’ opportunistic behaviour. Without such oversight, using EM strategies to secure abnormal remuneration will erode public trust.

title: DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION AND THE EVOLUTION OF EMPLOYMENT MODELS: CHALLENGES AND OPPORTUNITIES FOR EMERGING ECONOMIES
summary: This thesis examines how digital transformation reshapes employment models in emerging economies. Using conceptual and comparative analysis, it distinguishes changes in workplace tasks, digital job matching, and the governance of employment relationships. Particular attention is paid to remote work and platform-mediated employment, including opportunities for labor market participation and risks related to contractual uncertainty and social protection. The study proposes an analytical framework linking technological adoption, institutional readiness, and job quality. It outlines policy priorities for improving workforce adaptability and inclusive employment outcomes.

title: Dynamic carbon emissions and liquidity management under policy transition risks
summary: Liquidity is central to long-run green innovation under policy transition risk. We develop a dynamic model of carbon emissions and liquidity management for financially constrained firms under carbon policy transition risk. Our results show that greater policy transition risk promotes green innovation when cash liquidity is abundant, but reduces it when constrained. Furthermore, our paper reveals an inverted U-shaped relationship between policy stringency and green innovation. Moderate policy stringency promotes green innovation as the innovation-benefit effect dominates, whereas excessive stringency strengthens the liquidity-cost effect and discourages innovation by tightening firms' liquidity constraints. This finding provides theoretical support for the Porter Hypothesis and offers a potential explanation for the conflicting empirical evidence on the relationship between green innovation and environmental regulation.

title: Boundary Conditions of Institutional Investors' Impact on Stock Price Crash Risk
summary: Institutional investors are central participants in the capital market, and stock price crash risk is directly tied to the stability of that market. Existing studies mainly focus on how investors from institutions influence stock price crash risk, yet few studies summarize the boundary conditions under which this influence operates. This paper systematically reviews these boundary conditions from three dimensions: institutional investors' own heterogeneity, firms' own characteristics, and the external market and institutional environment. The literature review results indicate that under different boundary conditions, there are pronounced differences in the direction of institutional investors' impact on stock price crash risk (inhibition or exacerbation), as well as the strength of various mechanisms of influence. Finally, this paper identifies future research directions related to multi-boundary interaction effects and the ongoing reform of China's capital markets, providing a literature basis for deeply understanding the heterogeneous role of institutional investors and improving capital market regulation.

title: The Influence of Financial Shared Services on Accounting Information Comparability: Evidence from China’s Listed Manufacturing Firms
summary: Based on panel data of Chinese A-share listed manufacturing firms from 2015 to 2024, this paper explores the impacts and inner mechanisms of financial shared services on accounting information comparability. Results show financial sharing significantly improves accounting comparability; digital transformation strengthens this effect whereas controlling shareholder tunneling produces restraining influence, with earnings volatility acting as a partial mediator. Heterogeneous effects exist across firms grouped by ownership and executives’ overseas experience. This research offers practical suggestions for the differentiated construction of financial shared centers.

title: Managing climate stress for food security: the impact of rising temperatures on agricultural performance in Africa (1990–2022)
summary: Purpose Climate variation driven primarily by carbon emissions is a major driver of global warming, significantly raising Earth’s temperature. This study examines the influence of rising temperatures and carbon emissions on agricultural performance (AGP) in Africa from 1990 to 2022. The aim is to identify management policies that enhance sustainable agricultural resilience and moderate the adverse effects of climate change. Design/methodology/approach This research employs second-generation panel econometric techniques. The short- and long-run (LR) relationships between AGP, temperature, carbon emissions, sustainable finance and population growth are estimated using a Panel Autoregressive Distributed Lag (P-ARDL) model. Findings The results disclosed the fact that rising temperatures and carbon emissions significantly reduce AGP, highlighting the urgent need for proactive environmental management. Conversely, sustainable finance and population growth positively influence long-term AGP and food security. These variables emerge as crucial levers for climate adaptation and agricultural resilience across Africa. Practical implications Climate stress has made agricultural production more unpredictable and this threatens food security. The findings stress the need for integrated environmental and agricultural management policies. Hence, the study recommends that policymakers and financial institutions must prioritize investments in climate-smart agriculture and sustainable finance to address the challenges posed by climate variation, ensuring sustainable agricultural resilience and food security. Originality/value This study provides new evidence on the links between rising temperatures, carbon emissions, sustainable finance, population growth and AGP in Africa by jointly examining their short-run and LR dynamics within a panel framework, thereby offering policy-relevant insights for climate-resilient agricultural and financial strategies.

title: Entrepreneurial opportunity evaluation for financial technology decision
summary: Abstract Purpose Financial technology (FinTech) is increasingly associated with digital transformation and broader sustainability-oriented economic objectives. Although previous studies have extensively examined technological and organizational determinants of FinTech adoption, less attention has been given to the entrepreneurial cognitive processes associated with strategic technology investment decisions. This study examines the relationship between Entrepreneurial Opportunity Evaluation (EOE) and Financial Technology Decisions (FTD) among Thai financial institutions and assesses the mediating roles of Risk Re-Categorization (RRC), Financing Constraints Alleviation (FCA), Information Asymmetry Reduction (IAR), and Operational Efficiency Incentives (OEI). Design/methodology/approach A quantitative survey was conducted among Chief Financial Officers (CFOs) of firms listed on the Stock Exchange of Thailand (SET). Data were collected from 32 financial institutions and analyzed using Hayes’ PROCESS macro with bias corrected bootstrapping to examine the proposed mediation model. Findings The findings indicate that Entrepreneurial Opportunity Evaluation significantly influences Financial Technology Decisions both directly and indirectly. Risk Re Categorization, Financing Constraints Alleviation, and Information Asymmetry Reduction significantly mediate this relationship, whereas Operational Efficiency Incentives do not exhibit a significant mediating effect. Among the mediators, Financing Constraints Alleviation demonstrates the strongest indirect influence, suggesting that improved access to financial resources constitutes a primary strategic motivation for FinTech adoption within Thai financial institutions. Research limitations/implications The study is based on a relatively small sample of publicly listed financial institutions in Thailand, which may limit the generalizability of the findings. Future research should employ longitudinal and cross-country designs to examine how entrepreneurial opportunity evaluation influences digital transformation across different institutional contexts. Originality/value This study extends entrepreneurial cognition research by examining Entrepreneurial Opportunity Evaluation as an antecedent associated with strategic FinTech decisions. By integrating Resource Dependence Theory and Dynamic Capabilities Theory, it evaluates organizational mechanisms through which entrepreneurial evaluation is statistically linked to technology decisions. The sustainability discussion is framed as a broader implication rather than a directly measured outcome: the observed mechanisms may be relevant to financial inclusion, information transparency, organizational resilience, and sustainability-oriented digital transformation, particularly in relation to SDGs 8 and 9.

title: A relação entre a divulgação dos conteúdos das normas consolidadas do GRI e o valor de mercado das organizações da B3
summary: Este artigo tem como objetivo analisar se há diferenças significativas no valor de mercado associadas à evidenciação dos conteúdos das normas do GRI. A pesquisa caracteriza-se como descritiva e documental, sendo realizada a partir da análise dos relatórios de sustentabilidade de 216 empresas listadas na B3 em junho de 2024. Foi aplicado o teste de regressão com erros-padrão robustos, utilizando o software Stata®. Os resultados indicaram que a pontuação ESG total está positivamente associada ao valor de mercado das empresas. Isoladamente, os fatores Social e de Governança também apresentaram relação positiva e significativa com o valor de mercado, enquanto o fator Ambiental, apesar de apresentar coeficiente positivo, não demonstrou significância estatística. Como contribuição, este estudo amplia a compreensão sobre a relação entre práticas ESG e desempenho financeiro no Brasil, evidenciando as limitações da divulgação ambiental e apontando para lacunas de materialidade em alguns setores. Além disso, destaca a necessidade de aprofundamento em futuras pesquisas, sobretudo com foco setorial e análise longitudinal.

title: Digital Economic Expert Analysis as a New Type of Forensic Economic Examination in the Context of Digital Transformation
summary: The article justifies the need for the development of judicial economic expertise in the context of rising crimes involving cryptocurrency. It demonstrates that traditional types of economic expertise do not fully allow for the investigation of transactions with digital assets due to the specific nature of cryptocurrencies. The introduction of a new type of judicial economic expertise economic-digital — is proposed. Its purpose, tasks, object, and subject are defined, along with the methodology for conducting it. Particular attention is paid to the calculation of the weighted average price of cryptocurrency on the reporting date. A standardized tabular form is presented for summarizing results, enabling the identification of patterns in the movement of funds.

title: Sustainable Work Environments as Strategic Capabilities for Workforce Resilience: An Empirical Study of Listed Small Businesses in an Emerging Economy
summary: Abstract: Sustainable development has become a central concern for organizations operating in volatile and resource-constrained environments, yet the ways in which sustainable work environments contribute to workforce resilience in developing countries remain poorly understood. This study examines the effect of advancing sustainable work environments on workforce resilience among small businesses in an emerging economy, and situates the analysis within the broader agenda of sustainable development. The theoretical framework integrates the Resource-Based View (RBV), Social Exchange Theory (SET), and Dynamic Capabilities Theory, positioning employee-centred management practices as strategic organizational capabilities for resilience and long-term sustainability. Adopting an empirical, positivist approach, the study employed a quantitative cross-sectional survey design administered to 480 employees of small and medium-sized enterprises listed on the Nigerian Exchange (NGX) Growth Board. The multidimensional construct of sustainable work environments was operationalized across five core dimensions: work-life balance, work contentment, career growth, recognition and appreciation, and employee benefits. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, Pearson product-moment correlation, and multiple linear regression, and several procedural safeguards were applied to mitigate internal and common-method biases. The results revealed a very strong, statistically significant positive relationship between advancing sustainable work environments and workforce resilience (R = 0.936), with the five dimensions collectively explaining 87.7% of the variance in workforce resilience (R² = 0.877; F(5,399) = 568.400, p < 0.001). These findings demonstrate that repositioning sustainable workplace practices from routine human resource activities into strategic organizational capabilities significantly enhances employee adaptability and psychological resilience amid macroeconomic disruptions. The study advances understanding of sustainable development by showing that decent and sustainable work environments (SDG 8), employee health and well-being (SDG 3), and resilient, growth-oriented enterprises (SDG 9) are mutually reinforcing, and that investment in sustainable workplaces constitutes both a contribution to, and a mechanism for addressing the challenges of, sustainable development in emerging economies. The study offers contextual, theoretical, methodological, and empirical evidence from an under-represented African setting, and provides actionable insights for integrating workplace sustainability into Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) frameworks, corporate governance, and SME development policies. Overall, the evidence supports a conceptualization of sustainable work as a strategic investment that strengthens workforce resilience and organizational continuity, thereby aligning enterprise-level human resource practices with national and global sustainable development priorities. Keywords: Sustainable work environment; Workforce resilience; Small businesses; Listed companies; Strategic capabilities; Emerging economy; Sustainable human resource management (Sustainable HRM); Work-life balance; NGX Growth Board; Organizational resilience.

title: COMPETITIVIDADE INTERNACIONAL NÃO SE CONSTRÓI COM RETROCESSO: ESG, TRANSIÇÃO TECNOLÓGICA E QUALIFICAÇÃO CONTINUADA PRECISAM FAZER PARTE DA MESMA ESTRATÉGIA DE DESENVOLVIMENTO
summary: Este artigo examina em que condições a articulação entre ESG, transição tecnológica, qualificação continuada e tributação pode favorecer a competitividade internacional e o desenvolvimento humano sustentável. Adota o paradigma da complexidade e uma ontologia relacional e sistêmica, compreendendo organizações, trabalhadores, instituições, tecnologias e ambiente como dimensões interdependentes. A perspectiva transdisciplinar integra engenharia de produção, antropologia, administração empresarial, administração e políticas públicas, contabilidade e direito financeiro e tributário comparado. Desenvolve-se um ensaio teórico de abordagem qualitativa, sustentado em pesquisa bibliográfica e documental, atualização narrativa da literatura de 2024 a 2026 e comparação jurídico-institucional. A seleção prioriza pertinência temática, consistência metodológica e publicações em periódicos Q1, sem equiparar classificação editorial à validade de cada resultado. A análise relaciona eficiência de processos, aprendizagem, relações de poder, governança organizacional e capacidade estatal, distinguindo evidências publicadas de proposições dos autores. Sustenta-se que ganhos produtivos dependem de complementaridades entre tecnologia, competências, participação e coordenação institucional. Na tributação, recuperabilidade de créditos, ressarcimento e segurança jurídica condicionam os efeitos das alíquotas nominais sobre custos. Conclui-se que a competitividade sustentável requer estratégias empresariais e políticas públicas articuladas, com avaliação distributiva e socioambiental. As conclusões são condicionais; o estudo não produz estimativas causais próprias nem generalizações estatísticas.

title: Digital transformation in nursing education: students’ satisfaction, academic self-efficacy, and challenges with interactive e-books
summary: With the increasing integration of digital tools in nursing education, interactive e-books have emerged as innovative resources that promote engagement, flexibility, and active learning. However, evidence regarding their effectiveness in enhancing nursing students’ satisfaction and academic self-efficacy, as well as the challenges affecting their use, remains limited. This study aimed to assess nursing students’ satisfaction, academic self-efficacy, and perceived challenges related to the use of interactive e-books. A mixed-methods design was employed among 500 undergraduate nursing students at Capital University, Egypt. Quantitative data were collected using validated instruments measuring satisfaction and academic self-efficacy. Descriptive statistics and correlation analysis were used to examine relationships between variables, while multiple linear regression analysis was conducted to identify key predictors of both outcomes. In addition, qualitative data were collected using semi-structured questionnaires and analyzed thematically to explore students’ perceived challenges related to the use of interactive e-books. The majority of students reported high levels of satisfaction (72.2%) and self-efficacy (63%). A strong positive association was observed between satisfaction and self-efficacy. Multiple linear regression analysis identified academic performance (GPA) as a significant predictor of satisfaction (β = 0.185, p < 0.001) and self-efficacy (β = 0.198, p < 0.001). Prior training was also a significant predictor of satisfaction (β = 0.142, p = 0.014) and self-efficacy (β = 0.155, p = 0.005). Age and academic level were additionally significant predictors across both models, whereas gender was not statistically significant ( p > 0.05). The regression models explained a moderate proportion of variance in both outcomes, emphasizing the multifactorial nature of satisfaction and self-efficacy in technology-enhanced learning environments. Qualitative findings revealed key barriers, including technical limitations, content navigation difficulties, limited access to devices and internet connectivity, cognitive overload, and insufficient digital literacy. Interactive e-books can enhance nursing students’ satisfaction and self-efficacy; however, their effectiveness depends on students’ academic preparedness, technological accessibility, and system design. Addressing identified barriers and strengthening digital readiness are essential for optimizing the integration of interactive e-books in nursing education. Not applicable.

title: Balancing Mineral Extraction and Environmental Regulation: An Analysis of the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957 and the 2023 Amendment
summary: In recent past we have witnessed India's mineral sector being reshaped into a competitive commercial market, instead of its traditional image as a discretionary licensing system. The repeatedly amended Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957, with the recent amendments of 2015 and 2023, presently allocates mineral franchise largely through auctions, and has made available exploration and critical minerals to a wide private presence. This paper asks whether the amended Act, read with the surrounding environmental framework, balances mineral extraction against environmental protection legal system. It argues that the reforms have redesigned mining as a market while leaving environmental compliance outside the ambit of the incentive structure of that market, so that concession holders, who have the greatest control over environmental outcomes, face weak financial and governance incentives to comply. Using a doctrinal method, the paper tracks the statutory evolution of the Act, inspects the 2023 Amendment, reviews the judicial response, and then evaluates three management law mechanisms: auction design, the District Mineral Foundation alongside corporate social responsibility, and sustainability disclosure. It identifies five problems and suggests a corresponding reform for each: baseline screening at the exploration stage, earlier environmental scrutiny in the allocation process, environmental weighting in auctions, community-centred use of mining levies, and mine-level disclosure. Keywords: mining regulation; MMDR Act; 2023 Amendment; critical minerals; environmental governance; District Mineral Foundation.

title: Data Factor Agglomeration and Enterprise Resilience: Quasi-Experimental Evidence from China's National Big Data Comprehensive Pilot Zones
summary: Using the establishment of China's National Big Data Comprehensive Pilot Zones as a quasi-natural experiment, this study examines the effect of data factor agglomeration on enterprise resilience with a panel of A-share listed enterprises from 2012 to 2024. The results indicate that data factor agglomeration significantly improves enterprise resilience. The mechanism tests, interpreted alongside the theoretical analysis, provide evidence consistent with three channels: increased government subsidies, digital transformation, and stronger innovation capability. Executives' innovation awareness positively moderates the relationship between data factor agglomeration and enterprise resilience. Positive and statistically significant effects are observed among non-state-owned enterprises, enterprises in high-technology industries, and enterprises in eastern China; the corresponding estimates for state-owned enterprises, enterprises in non-high-technology industries, and enterprises in central and western China are not statistically significant. These findings suggest that policies should improve the conditions for data factor agglomeration, support enterprises' digital transformation, and account for differences in enterprises' characteristics when seeking to strengthen resilience.

title: Digital Transformation Implementation in Provincial Veterinary Office Services: Challenges, Opportunities, and its Impact on Service Delivery in Masbate Province
summary: This study evaluated the digital transformation of Provincial Veterinary Office (PVO) services in Masbate Province, focusing on its implementation, challenges, opportunities, perceived impact on service delivery, and strategic interventions. Employing a descriptive-survey research design, data were gathered using a researcher-made questionnaire administered to 47 respondents, including PVO personnel, LGU employees, and livestock raisers or farmers, and analyzed through frequency, percentage, and weighted mean. Findings indicated strong implementation across online service delivery systems, digital record management, communication technologies, and data collection systems. Despite these achievements, challenges persist regarding technological infrastructure, digital literacy, budget constraints, and technical support. However, respondents strongly acknowledged opportunities to enhance service speed, accessibility, transparency, and modern technology integration, noting positive impacts on overall service delivery efficiency, record accuracy, and client satisfaction. To sustain these improvements, respondents strongly supported strategic interventions, particularly continuous employee training, upgraded ICT infrastructure, and the adoption of integrated digital systems.

title: Revised Schedule M 2023 & Pharmaceutical GMP in India: Regulatory evolution, Compliance challenges, Digital transformation and Future perspective
summary: The new update to Schedule M under the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules is dated December 28, 2023. The update represents one of the most significant changes in India's Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) since they were introduced in 1988. In the course of this article, I will discuss the evolution of regulations. They were amended in 2001 and 2005, and now there is another revision of the GMP. This update aligns India's regulations with those of the World Health Organization (WHO) and the International Council for Harmonisation (ICH). In this article, we will analyze different aspects of the schedule such as pharmaceutical quality system, quality risk management, qualification and validation, change control, record-keeping, computerized systems use and specific requirements for various products that are presented in Parts 2-13. The article will pay attention to the challenges of implementing the new rules, particularly in the case of MSMEs. These companies usually face financial and human resource limitations, which may influence not only product quality but also integrity of data. The integration of digitalization, Industry 4.0, AI/ML technologies and continuous manufacturing into GMP requirements will also be discussed in this paper. The article will also provide an overview on the impact of the Coldrif cough syrup incident that occurred in India. This tragedy serves as an example of what can happen when GMP rules are not followed, and we'll look ahead at the future of Pharma 4.0.

title: Strategic Educational Leadership and Management Practices as Predictors of Institutional Effectiveness: A Framework for AI-Enabled Digital Transformation in Higher Education
summary: This study examined the predictive influence of strategic educational leadership and management practices on institutional effectiveness in selected higher education institutions and developed an artificial intelligence-enabled digital transformation framework based on the findings. Specifically, it assessed the levels of strategic educational leadership, management practices, and institutional effectiveness and determined whether leadership and management practices significantly predicted institutional effectiveness. A quantitative, non-experimental predictive-correlational research design was employed, involving 136 academic administrators selected through total enumeration. Data were collected using a validated and reliability-tested survey questionnaire and analyzed through weighted mean, standard deviation, and multiple linear regression at a 0.05 level of significance. The findings revealed high levels of strategic educational leadership (4.32), management practices (4.30), and institutional effectiveness (4.29). Regression analysis showed a strong predictive relationship, with a correlation coefficient of 0.870 and a coefficient of determination of 0.756, indicating that the independent variables explained 75.6% of the variance in institutional effectiveness. Both strategic educational leadership and management practices significantly and positively predicted institutional effectiveness, with regression coefficients of 0.431 and 0.440, respectively. The findings highlight the importance of effective leadership and sound management in improving institutional performance. The study concludes that strengthening these practices can enhance institutional effectiveness in higher education institutions. Based on the findings, an artificial intelligence-enabled digital transformation framework was developed to integrate strategic leadership, effective management, and artificial intelligence-driven innovations. The framework aims to support evidence-based decision-making, improve organizational processes, strengthen quality assurance, and promote continuous institutional improvement. Its implementation may help higher education institutions achieve sustainable effectiveness and respond to the evolving demands of digital education.

title: Supplier ESG Activities and Trust Formation in Sustainable B2B Supply Chains: A Dyadic Perspective
summary: ABSTRACT Environmental, social, and governance (ESG) activities have become increasingly important in sustainable supply chain management, yet limited research has examined how supplier ESG engagement influences interfirm trust and long‐term buyer–supplier relationships in B2B contexts. Drawing on 205 matched supplier–buyer dyads in South Korea, this study examines associations among supplier ESG activities, buyers' perceptions of warmth and competence, benevolence‐based and credibility‐based trust, long‐term orientation and relationship extendedness. The hypotheses were examined using covariance‐based structural equation modeling, supplemented by continuous moderation tests with heteroskedasticity‐robust standard errors and bootstrap confidence intervals. This study further examines buyer ESG awareness as a moderator of the associations between supplier ESG activities and relational perceptions. The findings show that environmental activities are positively associated with perceptions of warmth, whereas governance activities are positively associated with perceptions of competence. Both benevolence‐based and credibility‐based trust are positively associated with long‐term relational outcomes. The continuous moderation analysis identified one significant boundary condition: ESG awareness attenuated the association between supplier social activities and perceived warmth, supporting Hypothesis 8b. The remaining three moderation hypotheses were not supported. The study extends research on ESG‐related warmth and competence perceptions to B2B relationships by linking supplier‐reported activities with buyer‐reported perceptions, two dimensions of interfirm trust, and relational outcomes, while examining ESG awareness as a potential boundary condition. The findings identify cross‐sectional associations and do not establish a causal mediation process.

title: Tanggung Jawab Sosial, Etika Bisnis, dan Pemindaian Lingkungan Strategis dalam Manajemen Strategik: Sebuah Tinjauan Literatur
summary: Corporate social responsibility, business ethics, and the analysis of the strategic environment are two pillars that are often discussed separately, even though both determine the long-term sustainability of a firm within the discipline of strategic management. This study aims to synthesize recent scholarly literature examining these two pillars and to map the conceptual linkages between them. This research employs a narrative-thematic literature review method, drawing on articles published in internationally reputable journals indexed in Scopus (quartile Q1 to Q3) within the last three years (2023-2026), complemented by foundational theoretical works that continue to underpin the field. The review identifies five major themes: (1) the conceptual evolution and enduring debate surrounding corporate social responsibility; (2) the empirical relationship between social responsibility and financial performance; (3) ethical governance mechanisms, particularly whistleblowing, as instruments of organizational integrity; (4) environmental scanning and competitive strategy frameworks, particularly Porter’s Five Forces, as tools for reading the external environment; and (5) the intersection of social responsibility and industry competitiveness as a mediating pathway linking the two pillars. The findings indicate that social responsibility and environmental analysis are not two separate strategic activities, but two complementary capabilities that jointly determine a firm’s competitive advantage and organizational legitimacy. This study contributes theoretically by offering an integrative framework connecting business ethics literature with strategic analysis literature, and practically by providing managers with references for designing more comprehensive corporate strategies.

title: The Impact of Digital Transformation on Enterprise Performance
summary: Under the background of restructuring the global industrial chain and increasing downward pressure on the economy, there is no unified conclusion in the academic circle as to whether the digital transformation can break through the traditional "Solow paradox" and effectively stimulate the performance growth. Based on the panel data of China's A- share listed companies, this paper uses fixed effect model and intermediary effect test method to empirically analyze the impact of digital transformation on enterprise performance and the specific transmission mechanism. The research results show that digital transformation can obviously improve the business performance of enterprises. After a series of robustness and endogenous tests, this conclusion is still valid. The results of mechanism analysis show that digital transformation indirectly promotes performance improvement by optimizing the allocation efficiency of fixed assets, activating supply chain finance and enhancing supply chain toughness. Heterogeneity analysis further found that this boosting effect is more obvious in non-state-owned enterprises and high-tech industries. This research breaks the inherent cognition that performance loss is inevitable in the early stage of digital transformation, not only enriches the theoretical system of digital technology empowerment, but also solves the problem of resource mismatch for micro-enterprises, the realization of precise policy implementation by macro policies provides important empirical reference.

title: Saudi Arabian and Emirati Climate Diplomacy toward Pacific Island Countries: Motivations, Practices, and Limits
summary: Why do hydrocarbon-exporting states pursue climate diplomacy toward Pacific Island countries that call for an accelerated fossil-fuel transition? This article compares Saudi Arabian and Emirati engagement from 2010 to September 2026 through a qualitative analysis of official documents, regional communiques, climate-policy texts, project records, and scholarly literature. It combines status seeking, niche diplomacy, institutional assets, and recipient agency in a framework linking motivations, practices, and outcomes. The findings show that economic diversification, reputational pressures, and wider South-South engagement motivate both states, but their institutional resources generate different diplomatic pathways. The United Arab Emirates follows a project-technology-institution model based on renewable-energy delivery, specialized agencies, and multilateral platforms. Saudi Arabia follows a finance-forum-politics model centered on major pledges, ministerial convening, and high-level diplomatic outreach. Pacific Island countries filter both approaches through regional priorities, partnership rules, and fossil-fuel-free norms. Consequently, Gulf engagement has produced tangible functional benefits and some institutional access, but limited normative convergence. The article argues that climate finance becomes diplomatic influence only when commitments are implemented, embedded in Pacific-led institutions, and judged consistent with recipient-defined climate priorities. It thereby explains both the possibilities and the structural limits of hydrocarbon exporters' climate diplomacy in highly climate-vulnerable regions.

title: Green innovative behavior: impact of intrapreneurship and leadership
summary: Purpose Grounded in the componential theory of creativity (CTC) and extended through the lens of the theory of planned behavior (TPB), this study examines how employee intrapreneurship drives green innovative behavior (GIB) and innovative performance (IP). Specifically, it evaluates the moderating roles of individual moral reflectiveness (MR) and contextual ambidextrous leadership within Pakistan's hotel industry, a context where sustainability initiatives are still nascent and employee-driven green innovation remains largely unexplored. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected via a survey of 300 employees across 3-, 4-, and 5-star hotels in Lahore. Partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) was conducted using Smart PLS 3.0 to analyze the data. Findings Intrapreneurship positively influences both GIB and IP, with GIB serving as a key mediator. Crucially, moral reflectiveness counterintuitively weakens, rather than strengthens, the positive link between intrapreneurship and GIB, uncovering a novel boundary condition. Ambidextrous leadership exhibits no significant moderating effect. Practical implications The findings offer hotel managers a clear route to unlocking employees' green innovative potential. By identifying individual factors (intrapreneurship, moral reflectiveness) and contextual factors (ambidextrous leadership) that jointly shape GIB and innovative performance, the study provides actionable levers for designing sustainability-oriented HR and leadership strategies. Originality/value This study advances green organizational behavior by combining CTC and TPB to map MR as attitude, intrapreneurship as intention, and ambidextrous leadership as perceived behavioral control. By revealing the paradoxical dampening role of moral reflectiveness, it challenges conventional assumptions that moral traits universally foster eco-innovation.

title: Common ownership and consumer welfare
summary: Abstract Rival firms with shared institutional investors (i.e., common owners) may compete less aggressively, potentially harming consumer welfare. Yet, research on common ownership has primarily focused on firm performance, often overlooking welfare outcomes or revealing contradictory results. This paper adopts a strategic network perspective to examine how common ownership affects firms’ service quality and pricing levels, which directly impact consumer welfare, and how customer and competitor factors that alter the focus of competitive strategy moderate these effects. To test the hypotheses, the authors analyze a rich, multi-market dataset of U.S. airline firms from 1995 to 2025. Findings reveal that competing firms with higher common ownership tend to have lower service quality and set higher prices. However, this effect is attenuated for firms with high customer-asset value and amplified among rivals competing across multiple markets. The findings demonstrate common ownership’s influence on firms’ marketing mix strategies and offer actionable insights for managers, policymakers, and investors.

title: EFFECT OF SUSTAINABLE BUSINESS PRACTICES ON COMPETITIVE ADVANTAGE OF DEPOSIT MONEY BANKS
summary: This study examined the influence of sustainable business practices on competitive advantage in deposit money banks in Calabar. The specific objectives were to determine the effect of environmental sustainability practices on customer loyalty, economic sustainability practices on profitability, corporate governance and ethical practices on brand reputation among money deposit banks. The study adopted a quantitative research design using a cross-sectional survey approach. Primary data was collected through structured questionnaires administered to employees of selected deposit money banks under study. Data was analyzed using simple linear regression analysis at a 0.05 level of significance. Findings revealed that environmental sustainability practices have a significant positive effect on customer loyalty. Economic sustainability practices were found to have a significant positive effect on profitability. Corporate governance and ethical practices significantly influenced brand reputation. The results further indicated that all null hypotheses were rejected, confirming that sustainable business practices significantly enhance competitive advantage in deposit money banks. It recommended that banks should strengthen their environmental initiatives, enhance economic efficiency strategies, reinforce corporate governance systems, and expand customer-focused digital and sustainability-driven innovations.

title: Akuntabilitas dan Transparansi Pengelolaan Zakat Nasional: Analisis Laporan Pengelolaan Zakat Nasional Tahun 2023–2025
summary: This study analyzes the accountability and transparency of national zakat management in Indonesia based on the National Zakat Management Reports for the period 2023–2025. Employing a descriptive-comparative analysis of secondary data, the study compares year-on-year growth rates, disbursement-to-collection ratios (DCR), and reporting compliance ratios across the three reporting years. Rooted in agency theory and standard Islamic accounting (PSAK 109), the study evaluates institutional expansion, collection trends, disbursement effectiveness, and mustahiq socio-economic graduation. The findings reveal a significant increase in reporting compliance (97.33% in 2025) and collection growth reaching IDR 44.70 trillion, driven by digital transformation via SIMBA and NIK integration. Highly efficient disbursement ratios (89.93%–96.55% for on-balance sheet funds) and growing auditor compliance (175 audited OPZs in 2025) demonstrate strengthened public trust and reduced agency costs. ABSTRAK Kajian ini menganalisis akuntabilitas dan transparansi pengelolaan zakat nasional di Indonesia berdasarkan Laporan Pengelolaan Zakat Nasional periode 2023–2025. Penelitian ini menggunakan analisis deskriptif-komparatif terhadap data sekunder dengan membandingkan tingkat pertumbuhan tahunan, rasio penyaluran terhadap penghimpunan (DCR), dan rasio kepatuhan pelaporan antartahun. Berlandaskan teori keagenan dan standar akuntansi syariah (PSAK 109), penelitian ini mengevaluasi ekspansi kelembagaan, tren penghimpunan, efektivitas penyaluran, serta graduasi sosio ekonomi mustahik. Hasil kajian menunjukkan peningkatan signifikan pada kepatuhan pelaporan (97,33% pada 2025) dan pertumbuhan penghimpunan hingga mencapai Rp44,70 triliun, yang didorong oleh transformasi digital melalui SIMBA dan integrasi NIK. Rasio penyaluran yang sangat efisien (89,93%–96,55% untuk dana on-balance sheet) serta peningkatan kepatuhan audit (175 OPZ diaudit pada 2025) membuktikan semakin kuatnya kepercayaan publik dan menurunnya biaya keagenan.

title: Digital Accounting Disclosure and Market Valuation of Listed Non-Financial Companies in Nigeria
summary: The increasing use of digital technologies in accounting has changed not only how financial information is generated but also how companies communicate the quality and reliability of their reporting processes to capital-market participants. This study examines the relationship between digital accounting disclosure and market valuation of listed non-financial companies in Nigeria, focusing on real-time financial reporting disclosure, automated tax reporting disclosure and automated internal control disclosure. The study adopts an ex-post facto design and uses archival information from annual reports and corporate disclosures of 66 listed non-financial companies over 2016–2025. Market valuation is proxied by market capitalization growth, while firm size, measured as the natural logarithm of total assets, is included as a control variable. Disclosure indices are constructed from corporate reports. The reduced model was re-estimated from the underlying firm-year observations rather than transferring coefficients from the original seven variable model. Robust ordinary least squares estimates based on 538 complete observations show positive but statistically insignificant coefficients for real-time financial reporting disclosure (β = 0.515; p = .333), automated tax reporting disclosure (β = 0.889; p = .264), and automated internal control disclosure (β = 1.216; p = .492). The findings suggest that disclosure of these technologies, by itself, did not provide sufficiently strong incremental information to explain short-term market capitalization growth during the study period. The study concludes that the valuation relevance of digital accounting disclosure may depend on the credibility, depth and usefulness of the information communicated rather than disclosure presence alone.

title: The Blessed Accountant How Artificial Intelligence Reclaims Time, Eliminates Error, and Elevates Strategy
summary: The rapid advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming the accounting profession by automating routine tasks, improving data accuracy, and enabling more strategic decision-making. This paper, titled The Blessed Accountant: How Artificial Intelligence Reclaims Time, Eliminates Error, and Elevates Strategy, examines the evolving role of AI in modern accounting and its implications for accounting professionals, organizations, and financial management. AI-powered tools can streamline bookkeeping, invoice processing, bank reconciliations, tax compliance, fraud detection, and financial reporting, thereby reducing manual workloads and minimizing the risk of human error. Beyond operational efficiency, AI enables accountants to shift their focus from repetitive transactional activities toward analytical interpretation, strategic planning, risk management, and advisory services. The paper also explores the challenges associated with AI adoption, including data privacy, cybersecurity, algorithmic bias, implementation costs, technological dependence, and the need for continuous professional development. It emphasizes that AI should be viewed not as a replacement for accountants but as an enabling technology that strengthens professional judgment, ethical responsibility, and value creation. The effective integration of AI into accounting requires a balanced approach that combines technological innovation with human expertise, regulatory compliance, and appropriate governance mechanisms. The study concludes that AI has the potential to redefine accounting as a more efficient, accurate, and strategically oriented profession, provided that its adoption is guided by transparency, accountability, and responsible use. Ultimately, the future of accounting lies in the collaboration between intelligent technologies and skilled professionals, empowering accountants to deliver greater organizational value.

title: Sustainability as a Competitive Strategy in India’s Paint Industry: Regulatory Drivers, Firm Practices and an Integrative Framework
summary: India’s paint industry is undergoing its most significant restructuring in decades. Large new entrants have added substantial capacity, incumbent margins are under pressure, and ownership of a leading multinational subsidiary has changed hands. At the same time, regulation on lead content and plastic packaging, together with growing environmental awareness, is raising the importance of sustainability. This paper examines how sustainability is becoming a dimension of competitive strategy in the sector. It combines an integrative review of literature on competitive strategy, the natural-resource-based view, institutional theory and green innovation with a document analysis of regulatory texts, company sustainability reports and industry analyses published between 2016 and 2025. The findings show that regulation has established a baseline of compliance, particularly the 90 parts per million limit on lead in household and decorative paints. However, evidence of non-compliant lead paints on the market points to an enforcement gap. Leading firms have gone beyond compliance through renewable energy, water stewardship, low-emission products and packaging responsibility, but the depth of these practices varies considerably across firms. Building on these findings, the paper proposes a Sustainability–Competitiveness Pathway Framework linking regulatory push, market pull and competitive pressure to green capabilities and to economic, environmental and social outcomes. Four propositions and implications for managers and policymakers are presented.

title: The Moderating Role of Board Gender Diversity on the Safety Performance–Firm Financial Performance Nexus: Evidence from JSE-Listed Firms
summary: The mining industry remains one of the most hazardous industries globally, with occupational injuries and fatalities imposing significant operational and financial costs on companies. Although prior research has explored the impact of workplace safety on financial performance, limited attention has been devoted to the role of board gender diversity in influencing this relationship. This paper examines the association between safety performance and firm financial performance in 46 JSE-listed mining firms, considering the moderating role of board gender diversity. This study adopted an unbalanced panel dataset covering the period 2015 to 2025. Safety performance data were obtained from sustainability reports and integrated reports, while data on financial performance and board gender diversity were obtained from annual financial reports. A fixed effects model was adopted to establish the relationship between study variables, while the two-step system generalised method of moments was used as a robustness test. This study found a statistically significant negative association between the injury frequency rate and financial performance of JSE-listed mining firms, whereas the fatality frequency rate was not significantly associated with financial performance. The findings show that board gender diversity shapes the safety performance–firm financial performance relationship. This study contributes to the occupational safety and corporate governance literature by providing evidence on the governance conditions under which safety performance influences financial performance in the South African mining sector. title: Nonlinear Effects of Board Age on Corporate Social Responsibility in Vietnam: The Moderating Role of Product Market Competition
summary: ABSTRACT This study examines whether the relationship between average board age and corporate social responsibility (CSR) is nonlinear and whether product market competition conditions this relationship. Drawing on Upper Echelons Theory and stakeholder, agency, and institutional perspectives, we argue that increasing board age initially supports CSR through greater experience, stakeholder knowledge, and reputational awareness, but eventually constrains it as conservatism and risk aversion become more pronounced. Using 2201 firm‐year observations from 259 Vietnamese listed firms over 2015–2023, we estimate firm‐ and year‐fixed‐effects models and conduct extensive robustness and endogeneity analyses. The results reveal an inverted U ‐shaped relationship between board age and CSR. Because the estimated turning point is below the sample mean, most firms lie on the declining portion of the curve, producing a predominantly negative average association, especially for environmental and governance CSR. Product market competition serves as an important boundary condition: in less competitive industries (higher HHI), the negative effect associated with higher board age is weaker. The findings remain robust across alternative specifications, winsorized data, subgroup analyses, lagged models, fixed‐effects instrumental‐variable estimation, and two‐step system GMM. By integrating a threshold‐based account of board age with an external competitive boundary condition, this study explains when and why board demographics shape responsible corporate behavior in an emerging market.

title: Digital Financial Reporting Technologies and Financial Reporting Quality of Listed Manufacturing Firms in Nigeria: Evidence from Cloud Accounting, Real-Time Reporting and Artificial Intelligence Integration
summary: The rapid digitalisation of accounting functions has altered the way listed manufacturing firms in Nigeria capture transactions, process financial information and prepare corporate reports. While accounting automation is generally expected to strengthen reporting quality, the benefits of individual technologies may differ according to their depth of adoption, integration and organisational context. This study focuses specifically on three emerging dimensions of digital financial reporting technology—cloud accounting adoption, real-time financial reporting capability, and artificial intelligence and analytics integration—and examines their expected relationship with financial reporting quality among listed manufacturing firms in Nigeria. Financial reporting quality is operationalised through discretionary accruals, with lower discretionary accruals interpreted as evidence of higher reporting quality. The study is framed by agency theory and signalling theory. An ex post facto panel research design is proposed for the 2015–2024 period, using information obtained from published annual reports and audited financial statements of sampled listed manufacturing firms. The empirical model specifies discretionary accruals as a function of cloud accounting adoption, real-time financial reporting capability, artificial intelligence and analytics integration, and firm size. The Modified Jones Model provides the basis for estimating discretionary accruals. Existing evidence from the underlying broader accounting-automation study indicates negative associations for the three retained technology dimensions, with real-time financial reporting reaching conventional statistical significance in the original seven-variable specification, while cloud accounting and artificial intelligence/analytics did not reach the 5 percent threshold. However, those coefficients were estimated in the original seven-variable model and should not be reported as the final coefficients of the present reduced model until the reduced specification is re-estimated. The article therefore provides a complete publication-oriented framework while maintaining this empirical integrity. The study is expected to contribute to the Nigerian accounting-technology literature by isolating three increasingly important digital reporting capabilities and showing why adoption depth, system integration and organisational readiness matter for reporting quality.

title: BOARD CHARACTERISTICS, OWNERSHIP STRUCTURE, AND AUDIT RISK COMMUNICATION THROUGH KEY AUDIT MATTERS: THE MEDIATING ROLE OF OVERLAPPING AUDIT COMMITTEES FROM A RESOURCE DEPENDENCE THEORY PERSPECTIVE
summary: Purpose - This study examines how board characteristics and ownership structure shape audit risk communication through Key Audit Matters (KAM) disclosure, with particular attention to the mediating and coordinating role of Overlapped Audit Committees (OvAC). Drawing on Resource Dependence Theory, the study views corporate governance not merely as a monitoring mechanism but also as a source of knowledge, expertise, information access, and coordination capacity that may influence the quality and contextual richness of audit risk communication. Methodology - The study employs a qualitative empirical approach based on document analysis and cross-case comparison of Indonesian manufacturing firms over the 2022–2024 period. Data are derived from publicly available annual reports, corporate governance disclosures, audit committee information, and Key Audit Matters reported in independent auditor reports. The analysis combines thematic analysis with cross-case comparison to identify recurring patterns linking board characteristics, ownership structure, OvAC, and the characteristics of KAM-based audit risk communication. Findings - The findings indicate that audit risk communication through KAM is associated with the broader configuration of corporate governance resources rather than with audit risk alone. Firms characterised by stronger combinations of board independence, relevant expertise, and diversity tend to demonstrate more context-specific and informative KAM disclosures. Ownership structure also appears to shape monitoring incentives and transparency orientation. The cross-case analysis further suggests that OvAC may function as an information-coordination mechanism by facilitating knowledge sharing and information integration across governance functions. Conversely, limited coordination and highly concentrated governance structures tend to be associated with comparatively more standardised and less contextually detailed risk communication. Discussion and Implications - The study extends the application of Resource Dependence Theory to the KAM literature by explaining how governance resources can be transformed into audit risk communication through information integration and coordination. The findings suggest that the effectiveness of KAM disclosure should be assessed not only from the number of matters disclosed but also from its specificity, firm relevance, explanation of management judgment and uncertainty, and description of audit responses. Practically, the study highlights the importance of strengthening board expertise, governance coordination, and the effective functioning of audit committee structures to improve the transparency and informativeness of audit risk communication. For regulators and standard setters, the findings provide evidence that the quality of KAM communication is embedded within a broader corporate governance ecosystem.

title: An Explainable Early-Warning System for Financial Distress: Board Governance Capacity as a Predictive Signal
summary: The identification of corporate financial distress using accounting information is adversely affected by high inflation because the information quality of accounting ratios decreases significantly during rapid changes in price levels. Therefore, decision makers require non-monetary warning signals that can provide relevant information without being affected by inflationary noise. In this study, we develop an explainable early-warning system by combining a formative Board Governance Capacity Index (BGCI) with eight accounting ratios to evaluate non-financial companies listed on Borsa Istanbul. We collected company data for the period 2014–2023, comprising 1,642 firm-year observations from 190 firms. Financial distress is defined as the presence of qualified or adverse audit opinions or negative book equity. The BGCI consists of five publicly reported dimensions: board size, board independence, percentage of female directors, percentage of foreign directors, and external audit quality. We evaluate the performance of six machine learning classifiers using firm-grouped cross-validation, isotonic probability calibration, out-of-time evaluation, and TreeSHAP for feature attribution. Incorporating BGCI improves out-of-sample performance for all six classifiers, with the AUC of the benchmark logistic regression model increasing by 0.067 points, from 0.644 to 0.711, and the calibrated Brier score decreasing by 0.054. Component ablation analysis confirms that BGCI performs better than individual governance attributes. BGCI has the highest mean out-of-sample Shapley value among the nine predictors (0.696) and increases the pooled out-of-time AUC from 0.671 to 0.719. Fixed-effects logistic regression estimates controlling for firm size, sector, and year effects indicate that a one-unit increase in BGCI is associated with a 4.3-percentage-point reduction in the predicted probability of financial distress. Partitioning predictions by macroeconomic regime indicates that the additional AUC gain provided by BGCI increases significantly from 0.016 during periods of relatively low inflation to 0.118 during periods of relatively high inflation, thereby improving the accuracy of early-warning signals when conventional accounting-based signals become less reliable.

title: Cyber-resilient Industry 4.0: digital system failures,algorithmic bias and governance challenges for sustainable smart cities
summary: Objectives: This paper examines a central tension within Industry 4.0. Digitalisation can improve efficiency, monitoring capacity and decision making, but it also creates vulnerabilities linked to digital system failures, cyber incidents and algorithmic bias. The study analyses how these risks condition sustainable and resilient digital transformation in industrial environments and why they are relevant to smart cities. Prior work: The paper builds on research on Industry 4.0, digital transformation and productivity, together with studies on cyber physical systems, smart city security, Internet of Things (IoT) vulnerabilities, artificial intelligence (AI) enabled cyber defence and algorithmic governance. It connects these strands to move beyond technical performance and cybersecurity alone. Approach: The study follows a conceptual and analytical approach, supported by selected secondary evidence from Spain and the European context. Spain provides a contextual empirical anchor for illustrating the operational and social relevance of cyber risk, while the European framework supports the analysis of cybersecurity, algorithmic transparency, human oversight and AI governance. Results: The analysis shows that Industry 4.0 should not be assessed only through automation, efficiency or productivity gains. Its sustainability also depends on resilient digital infrastructures and on the governance conditions under which algorithmic systems are deployed. Under opacity, scale and limited accountability, such systems may amplify hidden biases and generate persistent harms in workforce management, supplier selection and investment allocation. Implications: The findings are relevant for researchers, policy makers and practitioners involved in smart industry and smart city strategies, as they stress the need to align innovation with resilience, accountability and organisational trust. Value: The paper contributes an integrated framework linking cyber resilience, algorithmic governance and social sustainability, showing that sustainable digital transformation requires both resilient infrastructures and accountable automated decisions.

title: STRATEGIC ALIGNMENT, STAKEHOLDER ENGAGEMENT AND ORGANISATIONAL PERFORMANCE OF THE TEA INDUSTRY IN KENYA: A CASE OF KABIANGA TEA FACTORY
summary: Kenya's tea industry, a leading foreign exchange earner, faces climate variability, certification demands from international buyers and volatile auction prices. Corporate social responsibility (CSR) is often proposed as a strategic response, yet evidence on how it is managed in farmer-owned factories under the Kenya Tea Development Agency (KTDA) remains scarce. This study examined the effect of strategic alignment and stakeholder engagement, as dimensions of CSR practice, on the organisational performance of Kabianga Tea Factory in Kericho County, Kenya. The study was anchored on Stakeholder Theory and supported by the Natural Resource-Based View. A descriptive case study design was adopted. From a target population of 805 factory managers, operational staff, farmer-members, community representatives and KTDA oversight personnel, a sample of 160 respondents was drawn through stratified random and purposive sampling. Data were collected using a pilot-tested structured questionnaire, which yielded 146 usable responses (91.25 per cent), and were analysed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation and linear regression. Both practices were rated favourably, with strategic alignment scoring a mean of 3.98 and stakeholder engagement 3.90, while organisational performance scored 3.76. Strategic alignment (r = 0.831) and stakeholder engagement (r = 0.819) had strong, positive and significant relationships with performance, and individually explained 69.1 and 67.1 per cent of its variation respectively (p < 0.001). Both remained significant predictors in the overall regression model, with stakeholder engagement (β = 0.324) and strategic alignment (β = 0.301) contributing distinctly to performance (p < 0.001). The study concludes that CSR improves performance when it is embedded in strategy and built on genuine, two-way relationships with stakeholders. It recommends that the factory write CSR objectives into its strategic plan and mission, tie CSR targets to board-reviewed performance indicators, and formalise grievance-resolution mechanisms for farmers, workers and communities.

title: The impact of digital transformation in management accounting on business performance: Evidence from an emerging market
summary: Digital transformation has become a strategic priority for modern enterprises; however, the organizational mechanisms through which it enhances business performance remain insufficiently understood. This study investigates how digital transformation in management accounting improves business performance by examining the mediating roles of management accounting information quality and management effectiveness. Data were collected from 312 enterprises in Vietnam and analyzed using Cronbach’s alpha, exploratory factor analysis (EFA), confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), and structural equation modeling (SEM). The results indicate that digital transformation has a strong positive effect on management accounting information quality (β = 0.816), which subsequently strengthens management effectiveness and enhances business performance. In addition, the significant direct and indirect effects provide evidence of partial mediation, demonstrating that digital transformation creates organizational value through multiple complementary mechanisms. The originality of this study lies in explaining the organizational mechanism through which digital transformation improves business performance by identifying management accounting information quality as the pivotal capability linking digital transformation to management effectiveness and organizational performance. The findings provide practical implications for managers and policymakers by suggesting that the success of digital transformation depends not only on technology adoption but also on the organization’s ability to transform digital capabilities into high-quality management accounting information that supports effective managerial decision-making and sustainable business performance.

title: The Role of Green Adaptability and Circular Economy in Encouraging Green Innovation in Batik SMEs in Pekalongan
summary: This study examines the relationship between Green Supply Chain Management (GSCM), Green Adaptability, Circular Economy, and Green Innovation in the context of batik small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in Pekalongan, Indonesia, a traditional cultural industry facing significant environmental challenges. Although GSCM is often considered important in sustainable business transformation, this study empirically tests the integration of these three constructs through Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) and finds that Green Adaptability significantly influences Circular Economy (β = 0.149, p < 0.001) and Green Innovation (β = 0.396, p < 0.001), while Circular Economy also positively contributes to Green Innovation (β = 0.119, p < 0.001). In contrast, GSCM does not significantly influence these three variables (p > 0.5). These findings indicate that in the context of batik SMEs, the implementation of GSCM practices tends to be operational in nature and has not yet developed into a strategic capability capable of supporting sustainable innovation. Theoretically, this study extends the application of Dynamic Capability Theory and the Resource-Based View by emphasizing that organizational adaptive capabilities are the primary drivers of green innovation compared to fragmented green supply chain practices. Its empirical contribution is also significant because it fills a research gap in traditional cultural industries that has received little attention in the sustainability and innovation literature. These findings provide practical implications for policymakers and business actors to focus on developing adaptive capabilities and circular production systems to strengthen green innovation and the sustainable competitiveness of batik SMEs.

title: STAKEHOLDER PERCEPTIONS OF CORPORATE SOCIAL RESPONSIBILITY INITIATIVES IN INDIA: INSTITUTIONAL PRESSURES, LEGITIMACY, AND IMPLICATIONS FOR RESPONSIBLE ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT
summary: Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) has become a central mechanism through which corporations respond to growing social and environmental expectations. In India, the introduction of mandatory CSR spending under the Companies Act, 2013 has further institutionalized CSR practices, while simultaneously intensifying debates regarding their authenticity and effectiveness. This study examines stakeholder perceptions of CSR initiatives in India, focusing on perceived transparency, accountability, alignment with community needs, and perceived contributions to social, economic, and environmental sustainability. Drawing on institutional theory and legitimacy theory, CSR is conceptualized as a socially constructed practice whose effectiveness is evaluated through stakeholder interpretation rather than objective performance indicators. Using survey data from 441 stakeholders and employing descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, and cluster analysis, the study identifies distinct perception-based patterns of CSR legitimacy. Findings reveal strong positive associations among perceived transparency, accountability, community alignment, and perceived CSR effectiveness, and identify two dominant stakeholder clusters: one perceiving CSR as symbolic and compliance-driven and another viewing CSR as substantive and sustainability-oriented. The study contributes to the literature on Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management by empirically demonstrating how institutional pressures shape CSR perceptions in emerging economies and by highlighting the importance of legitimacy-building mechanisms for effective and credible CSR implementation.

summary: Against the backdrop of accelerating digital transformation, the relationship between the development of the digital economy (DE) and urban low-carbon development (ULCD) has become an important issue in current research. title: Artificial intelligence as a driver of organizational digitalization: Benefits, conditions and challenges
summary: Abstract This theoretical article examines artificial intelligence in organizational digitalization. It distinguishes digitization, digitalization, and digital transformation, then combines sociotechnical theory with the dynamic capabilities perspective to explain how technology interacts with employees, routines, organizational structures and adaptation. The framework proposes that artificial intelligence supports transformation when aligned with strategy, integrated into processes and complemented by employee expertise, data and responsible governance. It highlights tensions involving discretion, bias, accountability and the fit between standardized systems and local practices. The article contributes propositions for empirical research and argues that AI’s value depends on integrating technical systems with human capabilities and organizational oversight. AI applications can automate repetitive tasks, analyze large amounts of data, personalize services and support decisions. However, their effects depend on data quality, employee skills, leadership commitment and the organizational context. For this reason, the article moves the focus beyond the simple adoption of AI and highlights the organizational capabilities and governance needed to integrate it responsibly. title: Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) Disclosure in Africa: Current State of Play
summary: ABSTRACT Purpose: This paper evaluates the operational landscape, regulatory architectures, and corporate adoption patterns of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) disclosures across four key African capital markets: South Africa, Nigeria, Ghana, and Kenya. Design/methodology/approach: Utilizing a multi-jurisdictional documentary review protocol across the period 2018–2025, regulatory instruments, listing requirements, national accounting codes, and corporate sustainability reports (N = 240 corporate firm-years) were evaluated against a 7-dimension structural framework. Findings: The results demonstrate significant institutional heterogeneity. South Africa exhibits a mature statutory regime anchored by King IV and mandatory JSE listing rules. Nigeria and Kenya are undergoing rapid regulatory formalization driven by Central Bank mandates and stock exchange sustainability principles, while Ghana maintains a predominantly voluntary framework. Across all markets, a substantial implementation gap persists between regulatory adoption and third-party assurance. title: Beyond greenwashing? The politics of meaning in sustainable finance
summary: Sustainable finance is a prominent but contested feature of contemporary investment landscapes. Disclosure-based frameworks that require financial actors to publicly report how sustainability is reflected in their investment products amplify this dynamic. Two distinct analytical orientations structure scholarly debate on sustainable finance and its transformative potential. Structural perspectives explain why such regulatory approaches operate within rather than against financial logic, while actor-centered perspectives document heterogeneous constellations through which sustainable finance is constructed. Yet, neither theorizes the compliance process through which the macro-level regulatory architecture is translated into micro-level meaning-making, and, vice versa, how the conditions of the translation process shape what definitions of sustainability become institutionalized at macro-level. This commentary argues that a discursive-institutionalist lens illuminates the link between both accounts by focusing on the ideational and discursive dimensions of the compliance process and proposes a research agenda organized around three interrelated questions: under what institutional conditions the meaning of sustainable finance is collectively negotiated; how geopolitical and geoeconomic factors function as discursive occasions for revising those meanings; and finally, what governance through ambiguous disclosure-based regulations actually accomplishes.

title: Implementasi Strategi sebagai Proses Integratif: Pengorganisasian, Penataan SDM, Kepemimpinan, dan Pembelajaran-Kontrol
summary: Strategy implementation is a critical point that determines whether strategic choices actually result in changes in organizational performance. This article aims to compile an integrative synthesis of how strategy is translated into action through four layers of mechanisms: strategy translation, organizational architecture, human orchestration, and learning-control. The research uses an integrative literature review method with the main sources Chapter 9 and Chapter 10 Wheelen and Hunger (2012), which are enriched by fourteen reputable scientific articles on strategy implementation, organizational design, middle management, leadership, culture, dynamic capabilities, and digital transformation. The analysis is carried out through concept extraction, mechanism grouping, cross-source comparison, and propositional synthesis. The results show that the effectiveness of implementation is primarily determined by the horizontal alignment between programs, budgets, processes, structures, capabilities, incentives, and cultures, as well as vertical alignment between corporate goals, unit goals, and individual behavior. Structure and staffing should not be treated as final administrative decisions, but rather as organizational hypotheses that are continuously tested through initial indicators, results, and feedback. The role of middle managers, sensemaking, emotion regulation, and data governance are becoming increasingly important in digital transformation. The article proposes a four-layer framework that can be used for the diagnosis of implementation readiness and the development of an empirical research agenda. digital.

Crucially, this audit intercepts the 3D Kakeya solution (Wang-Zahl, 2025/2026). Because the 127-page 3D proof inherently nests 2D Kakeya maximal functions as a defensive "low-dimensional reduction" boundary control, the permanent revocation of the 2D architecture automatically triggers a systemic default in the 3D logical supply chain. title: Digital Twins: Legal Foundations and Their Impact on the Transformation of Civil Circulation
summary: In the context of the rapid development of information and telecommunication technologies and the digital transformation of all spheres of society, the scientific and legal community is increasingly turning to the phenomenon of the “digital twin.” This article examines the legal foundations of digital twins in the context of the transformation of civil circulation in the digitalization of economic relations. It is noted that Russian legal science has not developed a unified approach to defining the concept of a digital twin and its place in the system of objects of civil rights. The authors conclude that it is necessary to establish a legal definition of a digital twin, differentiate it depending on the scope of application, and determine the legal status of a digital twin in the system of objects of civil rights.
