title: A SYSTEMATIC STUDY OF CORPORATE REPUTATION AND BRAND ATTITUDE THROUGH CORPORATE SOCIAL RESPONSIBILITY: HIGHLIGHTING THE ROLE OF TRANSPARENCY AS A MEDIATING FACTOR
summary: The purpose of this research is to understand more about the interactions between corporate social responsibility (CSR), corporate reputation (CR), and brand attitude (BA) at work. This article lays out a theoretical framework based on the company's resource-based theory. Customer Transparency in this framework is designed to build CR and brand attitude, both directly and indirectly, through CSR. We used a questionnaire survey as a strategy. The survey had 17 items and was graded on a five-point Likert scale (1 representing "strongly disagree" and 5 representing "strongly agree"). The data was acquired from banking users in Pakistan's Lahore region. We estimate the hypothesized links in the conceptual model using Smart PLS 3.2 and structural equation modelling (SEM). CSR has a significant impact on customer retention and brand attitude, according to the findings of this study. In the relationship between CSR, CR, and BA, Transparency has been proven to play a positive and significant effect. The conclusions of this study have a wide range of implications for senior management, marketing professionals, administrators, and policymakers. This study demonstrates how CSR enhances BA and CR. Furthermore, this study reveals that Transparency plays an important role in boosting BA and CR.

title: Mapping institutional change research in higher education: A BERTopic-based topic modelling study
summary: Research on institutional change in higher education has grown quickly, but it remains fragmented across disciplines and theoretical traditions. This study maps the thematic structure of this research in educational sciences and traces how it has changed over 34 years. I analysed the titles and abstracts of 2,623 publications indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection (Education & Educational Research, 1992–2025) with BERTopic, an embedding-based topic modelling tool. Placeholder masking kept the names of countries, nationalities and languages from shaping the topics, and key model settings are reported for reproducibility. The model produced 24 interpretable topics covering 1,824 publications. The general Structural Reforms topic fell from 65.6% of topic-assigned publications in 1992–2000 to 12.5% in 2023–2025, while more specific themes such as sustainability, transformational leadership and diversity, equity and inclusion gained weight. In 2023–2025, Digital Transformation became the largest topic (14.8%), and Artificial Intelligence Integration rose from almost zero to 8.1%. Technology-related research developed in successive waves: e-learning, emergency remote teaching during the COVID-19 pandemic, digital transformation and generative artificial intelligence. Each wave reframed digitalisation with new concepts instead of simply continuing the previous one. These results suggest that institutional change in higher education is studied through several parallel pathways rather than a single dominant narrative. For policymakers and institutional leaders, the findings point to the need to build the capacity for change as a lasting institutional capability rather than responding to each technological, sociological and political disruption separately.

title: Supply chain agility enablers and SME performance: The roles of supply chain risk management performance and risk management culture
summary: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractThis study examines associations between three proactive enablers of supply chain agility, SME performance, and supply chain risk management performance, and assesses the mediating and moderating roles of supply chain risk management performance and risk management culture. Data were collected through an online survey using convenience sampling and analyzed via PLS-SEM. The study included 224 SMEs operating in the West Bank, Palestine. The findings indicated that market sensing (β = 0.358, p < 0.01) and supply chain integration (β = 0.318, p < 0.01) were positively and significantly associated with SME performance. In contrast, strategic sourcing (β = 0.050, p > 0.05) was not significant. Market sensing (β = 0.383, p < 0.01), strategic sourcing (β = 0.311, p < 0.01), and supply chain integration (β = 0.321, p < 0.01) were positively and significantly related to supply chain risk management performance. Supply chain risk management performance (β = 0.626, p < 0.01) was significantly related to SME performance. The results showed no moderating effect of risk management culture on the relationships between the three supply chain agility enablers and supply chain risk management performance (p > 0.05). Supply chain risk management performance significantly mediated the relationships between all three enablers and SME performance, with full mediation for strategic sourcing and partial mediation for supply chain integration and market sensing. Moreover, the model explains 77.3% of the variance in SME performance (R² = 0.773) and 61.3% of the variance in supply chain risk management performance (R² = 0.613).

title: Transformation of documentation support in the digital economy: the historical aspect
summary: Traditional document management methods are giving way to electronic systems integrated with business processes, as the conditions of digitalization inevitably introduce drastic changes in approaches to information management. The purpose of the article is to analyze current trends and challenges in the era of global digitalization, identify promising areas of development and identify progressive models of transformation of documentation support to improve the efficiency of document management in organizations. The relevance of the work is due to the need to adapt traditional office management systems to the requirements of automation, end-to-end data management and ensuring the legal significance of electronic document management. The research objectives include: reconstructing the current state of documentation support as a historically constituted institution entering a new phase of transformation on the path toward digital platforms; uncovering the inner logic of the transition from paper-based and hybrid document flow to a fully digital model built on unified repositories and API integrations — a transition comparable, in the scale of its institutional consequences, to earlier stages in the unification of Russian record-keeping; assessing the impact of digital technologies on the reliability and speed of document processing, as well as determining the specifics of digital transformation's impact on the processes of value appraisal, storage, and use of archival documents and other materials generated within electronic document flow systems. The research uses methods of theoretical analysis, synthesis, search, selection, systematization of sources, and comparison of research results from leading Russian companies. The methods of content analysis and case study were used to systematize the data. A problematic research field on the problems and prospects of transformation of documentation support for business process management in the digital economy is analyzed. A particular place in the article is occupied by the historical dimension of document flow: its digital transformation is treated not as an isolated technical and managerial phenomenon, but as another — and by no means final — link in the centuries-long chain of transformations of Russian document flow, from the prikaznoe record-keeping of the Muscovite state and the kollezhskoe system codified by the General Regulations of 1720, to the unified state record-keeping systems of the Soviet period (the Unified State Records System of 1973, the State System of Documentation Support for Management of 1988). Such a historical-genetic perspective allows the digitalization of document flow to be seen not as a break with tradition, but as its logical continuation.

title: Effect of Asset Diversification on Financial Performance of Deposit-Taking SACCOs in Kenya: The Moderating Role of Corporate Governance
summary: This study examined the effect of asset diversification on the financial performance of deposit-taking SACCOs (DT-SACCOs) in Kenya and the moderating role of corporate governance in this relationship. A positivist philosophy and an explanatory longitudinal design were adopted. Secondary panel data for 2015–2024 were extracted from the audited financial statements of 122 DT-SACCOs and SASRA reports. Asset diversification was measured by loans and non-loan assets as shares of total assets, financial performance by surplus and the dividend payout ratio, and corporate governance by a board accountability index. Fixed-effects (surplus) and random effects (dividend payout) panel models, selected by the Hausman test, and hierarchical moderated regression were estimated. The loan share was positively associated with surplus (β = 0.382, p < 0.01) but not with dividend payout, while the non-loan asset share was negatively associated with dividend payout (β = −0.092, p < 0.05). Board accountability was positively associated with both measures and strengthened the association of lending with surplus (β = 3.271, p < 0.01) and of non-loan assets with dividend payout (β = 0.130, p < 0.05). The results are associations based on secondary data, and governance is captured only through board meeting activity. The SACCO boards should treat member lending as the core business, appraise non-loan investments rigorously and strengthen board and audit committee accountability, while SASRA should monitor non-core investments.

title: MANAGING DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION IN SECONDARY SCHOOLS: A COMPARATIVE STUDY OF CHINA AND KAZAKHSTAN
summary: Worldwide, digital change is central to education modernization. For secondary schools, it involves more than computers, internet and digital platforms. It reshapes school governance, educational leadership, classroom practice, teacher development, data management and organizational culture. This paper compares digital‑transformation management in Chinese and Kazakh secondary schools. Drawing on policies and existing literature, it analyses national digital‑education strategies, infrastructure, teaching platforms, teachers’ digital skills, school leadership, data governance and digital equity. Both countries prioritize digital reform for educational modernization under different institutional backgrounds. China applies a centralized service‑driven model exemplified by the National Smart Education Platform. Kazakhstan integrates school digitalization into national education and digital‑economy strategies. They share common challenges: uneven digital infrastructure, varying teacher digital skills, data‑management troubles, cybersecurity threats and insufficient digital leadership at school level. Technical investment alone cannot guarantee successful transformation. School leaders need to combine digital tools with strategic planning, teacher training, institutional adjustment and evidence‑based decision‑making.

title: Data-Driven Closed-Loop System for Precise Ideological and Political Education in Higher Education
summary: Traditional ideological and political education in higher education faces delayed feedback and insufficient personalization amid digital transformation–driven fragmented, heterogeneous data. This manuscript addresses data integration, algorithm transparency, and privacy compliance bottlenecks via a data-driven closed-loop precise guidance system. Integrating extract, transform, load processing, feature selection, an Extreme Gradient Boosting–Long Short-Term Memory dual-channel model, state machine scheduling, and a five-level risk classification system, the system ensures interpretability via Shapley values and privacy compliance through dual signatures. Eight-week tests on 2,186 undergraduates across 12 universities showed 23.4-percentage-point higher engagement, a 4.8% false alarm rate, and a 31-s closed-loop processing time. Gradual intervention (Model A) outperformed a high-intensity intervention (Model B) in cost-effectiveness, with long-term follow-up confirming sustained stability. This study provides a replicable, ethical, and practical framework for digital ideological and political education.

title: Exploring the Nexus between Housing Prices, Environmental Taxation, Green Technological Innovation, and Environmental Sustainability: Evidence from the U.S. Building Sector
summary: This study aims to explore the impact of environmental taxation (ET) and technological innovation on carbon emissions. This study fills a critical gap in the existing environmental and finance literature by highlighting the effects of housing prices on carbon emissions within the United States building sector over the period from 1994 to 2021. The study employed the novel Augmented Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) method to assess the link between the tested variables. The study found that green technological innovation and ET positively affect carbon emissions reduction in the building sector, suggesting their positive role in enhancing ecological sustainability. Conversely, housing prices show a positive effect on carbon emissions from the building sector, emphasizing the critical need for ecological neutrality policies and the adoption of green energy alternatives in the building sector. The empirical quantification of HP’s long-run impact on building-sector CO 2 emissions constitutes a novel, robust, and policy-consequential finding that fundamentally challenges the implicit assumption that housing market conditions are environmentally neutral, establishing that no credible building-sector emissions reduction strategy can be designed without explicitly accounting for housing market dynamics. Therefore, based on these outcomes, this research provides implications for policymakers aimed at fostering a better environment in the building sector. The strategies and policies to reduce CO 2 in the building sector include enforcing standards and regulations such as ET, conducting impact assessments of housing prices, adopting green technologies, and restricting non-clean energy utilization.

title: E-Governance, Public Sector Performance and Gender Inclusion in Nigeria: A Conceptual Synthesis
summary: This paper examines how electronic governance (e-governance) and gender inclusion jointly shape the performance of Nigeria's public sector. Drawing on recent scholarship on public administration reform, administrative accountability, Management Information Systems (MIS) and women's leadership, it argues that digital transformation improves public service delivery only when it is paired with institutional accountability and deliberate gender-responsive design. A conceptual model links Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI), accountable administrative institutions and gender-inclusive policy to public sector performance and, ultimately, to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and the African Union's Agenda 2063. The paper identifies infrastructural, institutional and social constraints, including uneven digital access, rural isolation and persistent gender gaps, and proposes a four-step policy roadmap. The analysis is conceptual and synthesizes published literature; it does not report new primary data.

title: Rethinking physician–patient communication: exploring physicians’ use of AI in healthcare: a dual-factor perspective
summary: Purpose This study aims to identify the physicians’ intentions to use artificial intelligence (AI) in order to provide digital information to physicians about their patients by the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology 2 and QSB theories. Design/methodology/approach To collect the necessary data, an electronic questionnaire was designed to survey 789 physicians working in Iraqi clinics and healthcare institutions. To analyze these data, a structural equation model was used using the AMOS.26 program. Findings The results revealed the importance of the study model in using AI technology in communication between physicians and patients. Research limitations/implications It is concluded that communication between physicians and their patients should be based on the use of AI technology, as the vast majority of physicians surveyed supported this. This indicates the need to use AI technology and its digital tools in physicians’ performance of their healthcare tasks (consultations, examinations) and, consequently, in providing treatment to patients. Furthermore, this study is not without its limitations, namely its focus on AI. Thus, it should focus on other digital technologies. Originality/value This research provides innovative value by bridging the digital transformation gap in digital healthcare systems for patients. It is the first study in Iraq to re-establish communication between physicians and their patients. This study explains the importance of using digital technologies, such as AI, in providing healthcare to patients from a dual-factor perspective (motivation and inhibition), thus contributing to bridge the emerging gaps in healthcare services provided to patients.

title: Governance as the Key Question of the Coming Years: A Scholarly Dialogue With Guilherme Canela on Freedom of Expression, Artificial Intelligence, and the Future of Information Governance
summary: In this scholarly dialogue for Media, Technology, and Governance , Guilherme Canela reflects on the centrality of governance in contemporary debates over media, technology, and the global information ecosystem. Drawing on his long-standing work with journalists, governments, civil society, regulators, judges, researchers, and international organizations, Canela situates freedom of expression, access to information, and digital transformation within a broader human rights framework. The conversation begins with Canela's professional trajectory from Latin America to UNESCO headquarters in Paris, then turns to the challenges posed by generative artificial intelligence, platform power, journalism's economic viability, and the need for multistakeholder governance. Canela argues that although technologies change, the principles of journalism, human rights, transparency, accountability, and meaningful participation remain essential. He also calls for scholars to study information and journalism as public goods, the growing attacks on accountability systems, and the ways academic evidence can inform policymaking without sacrificing independence. The dialogue concludes with a message to researchers: governance is the key topic of the coming years, and the academic community is needed to provide the evidence, concepts, and critical debate required to meet that challenge.

title: Explaining Civil Servant Performance In The Digital Government Era: The Roles of Digital Competence, Preventive Discipline and Work Motivation
summary: This study examines the effects of digital competence, preventive discipline, and work motivation on employee performance at the Riau Provincial Manpower and Transmigration Office. A quantitative approach was employed, involving 135 State Civil Apparatus employees selected using a saturated sampling technique. Data were collected through questionnaires and analyzed using multiple linear regression with SmartPLS 4. The results indicate that digital competence has a positive and significant effect on employee performance (β = 0.357, t = 7.051, p < 0.001). Preventive discipline also has a positive and significant effect (β = 0.293, t = 5.395, p < 0.001), as does work motivation (β = 0.215, t = 4.377, p < 0.001). Collectively, these three variables significantly affect employee performance (F = 50.242, p < 0.001). The coefficient of determination (R² = 0.535) indicates that the three independent variables explain 53.5% of the variance in employee performance, while the remaining 46.5% is explained by factors outside the research model. These findings underscore the importance of strengthening digital competence, promoting preventive discipline, and enhancing work motivation to improve employee performance in government organizations undergoing digital transformation.

title: Digital Transformation in Personal Protective Equipment Management: Design and Implementation of a Web-Based Digital Custody and Audit Trail System
summary: Paper-based personal protective equipment (PPE) custody documentation remains widespread in Turkish small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and public institutions despite traceability obligations under the Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) Law No. 6331, generating recordretention vulnerabilities and audit liability risks. Adopting a Design Science Research (DSR) framework, this study presents a web-based PPE digital custody artifact evaluated against three legislatively grounded design criteria: audit integrity (C1), regulatory compatibility (C2), and institutional adoptability (C3). The artifact operationalizes Walsh and Ungson’s organizational memory framework, transferring custody records from individual-dependent and physically vulnerable repositories to a relational database, markedly reducing staff-departure and archive-destruction failure modes. Indicative process measurements (n=15 digital transactions against an n=3 paper baseline) yield reductions of approximately 87% in record generation time and 94% in archive retrieval time, pending larger-sample replication. Normative legal analysis establishes that Canvas-based handwritten signatures constitute a simple electronic signature recognized under EU eIDAS, US ESIGN/UETA, and Turkish Law No. 5070. Although not a qualified-signature equivalent, the composite audit trail can serve as an evidentiary record where public key infrastructure (PKI) is absent, subject to judicial determination. Twelve role-based access control (RBAC) functional test cases confirm that the hierarchical architecture enforces the separation of duties required by Law No. 6331. The findings provide a replicable artifact specification and a DSR evaluation template for the OHS management information system (OHS-MIS) deployment in resource-constrained settings.

title: THE IMPACT OF DIGITAL HRM PRACTICES ON EMPLOYEE WELL-BEING: THE MEDIATING ROLE OF KNOWLEDGE SHARING AND THE MODERATING ROLE OF TECHNOLOGICAL READINESS IN VIRTUAL WORK ENVIRONMENTS
summary: In the digital age, organizations are increasingly leveraging Digital Human Resource Management (DHRM) for improved performance and flexibility,yet this shift comes with issues such as digital fatigue and social isolation in virtual workplaces. This research seeks to explore the effect of Digital HRM on employee well-being (EWB), as well as the mediating effect of Knowledge Sharing (KS) and moderating effect of Technological Readiness (TR). Employing a quantitative, cross-sectional approach, primary data were collected through structured online surveys from 297 employees in the IT and banking industries in Islamabad and Rawalpindi, Pakistan. The results suggest that the effect of DHRM on knowledge sharing is positive and significant (beta = 0.184, p = 0.001), which leads to improved well-being (beta = 0.268, p = 0.000). Knowledge sharing partially mediates the relationship between DHRM and well-being (beta = 0.049, p = 0.011), and technological readiness significantly moderates the relationship between DHRM and knowledge sharing (beta = 0.102, p = 0.001). This study adds theoretically by combining Social Exchange Theory and the Technology Acceptance Model to explain psychological responses. Practically, it suggests that HR managers should consider employee technological readiness and trust for optimizing the impact of a digital transformation on employee well-being.

title: Reconstruction of Islamic Green Banking: Fiqh Al-Bi’ah As A Model Of Sustainable Islamic Finance
summary: Despite the growth of green financing, Islamic banking remains largely reliant on secular Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) frameworks, overlooking the normative foundations of Fiqh al-Bi’ah (Islamic environmental jurisprudence). This study reconstructs an Islamic green banking model grounded in Fiqh al-Bi’ah to advance Sustainable Islamic Finance. Using a qualitative socio-legal approach, it combines bibliometric analysis, Natural Language Processing (NLP), and Ijtihadi Maqashidi analysis to examine 34 Indonesian Islamic banks from 2017 to 2024. NLP-based text mining reveals isomorphic mimicry, with Fiqh al-Bi’ah terminology appearing in less than 1% of sustainability reports. In response, the study proposes an operational model integrating principles such as fasād, mīzān, and ḥimā into banking mechanisms, including Eco-Haram Screening, Maqasid-based Credit Scoring, and Conservation-Linked Financing. The model offers a framework for regulators and Sharia standard-setters to shift Islamic banking from compliance-based practices toward value-based sustainable finance.

title: Manufacturing Enterprises' Digital Asset Value Evaluation Based on Multi-period Excess Return Method and Case Analysis
summary: Data assets have become strategic resources for manufacturing enterprises due to digital transformation, but most remain off-balance-sheet, challenging stakeholders to evaluate their true value. Traditional methods like market and cost approaches fail to capture the dynamic nature of data assets, while the income approach still has limitations in predicting future earnings and discount rates. This work integrates the Multi-Period Excess Return Method (MPEEM) with the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) to accurately assess the value of data assets. The MPEEM isolates excess returns from data assets, and AHP separates the contribution of off-balance-sheet assets. Empirical analysis of Midea Group, BYD and Xiaomi shows that data assets significantly contribute to enterprise value, with core drivers including smart manufacturing data, consumer behavior analyses, and supply chain optimization data. This paper provides a robust framework for valuing data assets, supporting strategic decision-making and regulatory compliance in the manufacturing sector.

title: Taxes on Goods and Services and the Ecological Footprint: The Role of Digitalization
summary: The increasing urgency of climate change amid a rapidly evolving digital transformation underscores the need for integrated fiscal and technological policy to mitigate environmental degradation. This study examines the association between taxes on goods and services (TGS) and ecological footprint (EFP), and evaluates the moderating role of digitalization. Using a newly compiled dataset for 96 countries over the period 2000–2022, the analysis employs a cross-sectionally augmented autoregressive distributed lag (CS-ARDL). The results reveal a significant negative long-run association between TGS and EFP, suggesting a potentially important link between TGS and ecological pressure. Digitalization is positively associated with EFP, while the interaction results indicate that greater digitalization is associated with a stronger negative relationship between TGS and EFP. However, heterogeneity analysis reveals that these relationships are more noticeable in higher-income economies, while they remain weaker in lower-income countries. Complementary estimations using Common Correlated Effects Mean Group (CCEMG) and Augmented Mean Group (AMG) estimators, along with an alternative measure of the key explanatory variable, yield consistent findings. Overall, the study highlights the potential importance of considering digitalization within fiscal policy frameworks aimed at supporting ecological sustainability.

title: Beyond firewalls: public integrity and cyber resilience in European smart city governance
summary: This study examines how the level of public sector integrity influences cyber resilience and the security of digital governance in smart city environments across Europe. The research aims to move beyond a purely technological understanding of cybersecurity by demonstrating that smart city resilience also depends on transparent public procurement, accountable institutional oversight, reliable data governance, and the public sector’s capacity to govern complex digital infrastructures. The study builds on existing concepts of public sector integrity, cyber resilience, digital governance, and smart city governance, with particular attention to the relationship between corruption risks, supplier dependency, vendor lock-in, and the institutional conditions required for secure digital transformation. The research employs a comparative, indicator-based approach. It examines six European countries—Denmark, Finland, Estonia, Hungary, Romania, and Bulgaria—using public sector integrity indicators, cyber resilience indices, digital governance indicators, and public procurement risk proxies. As complementary explanatory dimensions, the analysis also considers supplier concentration, public procurement competition, and institutional control mechanisms. The findings suggest that, in the cases of Denmark, Finland, and Estonia, relatively high levels of public sector integrity are associated with strong cyber resilience and advanced digital governance capacity. Hungary and Romania display mixed profiles: both countries possess relatively strong formal cybersecurity capacities, while their integrity and public procurement indicators point to institutional vulnerabilities. Bulgaria emerges as the most vulnerable case among the countries examined, combining weaker integrity, lower cyber resilience, and more limited institutional control. The conclusions are relevant for researchers, policymakers, and practitioners alike, as they highlight that smart city cybersecurity cannot be ensured solely through firewalls and technical solutions. The study’s main contribution lies in integrating public sector integrity, public procurement governance, and cyber resilience within a common analytical framework for assessing the security of smart city governance in Europe.

title: Reimagining Public Administration, Governance, and Gender Policy in the Nigerian Landscape
summary: This paper presents a comprehensive, interdisciplinary evaluation of the intersecting dynamics defining contemporary Nigerian governance, specifically focusing on the nexus of institutional efficiency, digital transformation, spatial infrastructure, and gender-inclusive policy frameworks. Operating within the systemic realities of a developing federal state, public administration in Nigeria faces structural bottlenecks rooted in historical bureaucratic centralization, resource misallocation, and complex demographic demands. This study synthesizes a broad spectrum of recent empirical literature and theoretical models to highlight critical pathways toward robust public service delivery, operational transparency, and macro-level socio-economic equity. By critically analyzing systemic performance determinants, the adoption of Management Information Systems (MIS), and the challenges of electronic governance, the paper illustrates that administrative reform cannot successfully occur in isolation. Instead, long-term development requires a strategic, unified convergence of robust Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI), data-driven rural-urban spatial planning, and targeted gender empowerment models that address systemic marginalization. Ultimately, this study provides actionable theoretical frameworks and policy reference points aimed at aligning Nigeria's domestic administrative capacities with global development benchmarks, including the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and the African Union’s Agenda 2063.

title: FUNCTIONING OF STEM EDUCATION IN PEDAGOGICAL INSTITUTIONS OF HIGHER EDUCATION OF UKRAINE IN WARTIME CONDITIONS: PROBLEMS AND PROSPECTS FOR DEVELOPMENT
summary: The article examines contemporary challenges in the functioning of STEM education within the system of higher pedagogical education in Ukraine under wartime conditions. The relevance of the study is determined by the need to ensure the continuity and quality of professional preparation of prospective teachers of natural sciences, mathematics, computer science, and technology amid the destruction and relocation of educational infrastructure, academic staff losses, unequal access to laboratory and digital resources, accelerated digital transformation, and the need to prepare the Ukrainian education system for post-war recovery. The aim of the article is to comprehensively identify and systematize the key challenges affecting the development of STEM education in Ukrainian pedagogical higher education institutions under wartime conditions, determine the interrelationships among these challenges, and substantiate a conceptual model of STEM teacher education. To achieve this aim, the study employed a systematic analysis of scholarly publications and regulatory and policy documents, comparative-pedagogical, structural-functional, and problem-oriented analysis, as well as methods of systematization, generalization, classification, and modelling. The methodological framework of the study is based on conceptualizing STEM education as an integrated and multidimensional system whose effective functioning depends on the interaction of institutional, human-resource, infrastructural and resource, digital, psychological-pedagogical, and methodological factors. The main results demonstrate the existence of six interrelated groups of challenges affecting STEM education in Ukrainian pedagogical higher education institutions: organizational and institutional, infrastructural and resource, human-resource, digital and technological, psychological and pedagogical, and methodological challenges. The findings indicate that wartime conditions not only exacerbate existing challenges in STEM teacher education but also generate new requirements for the organization of the educational process, particularly regarding flexibility, the provision of distance and blended learning, digital security, the psychological resilience of educational participants, the development of international partnerships, and the continuity of professional preparation. On this basis, a conceptual model for the functioning of STEM education was substantiated, integrating regulatory and legal, organizational, human-resource, infrastructural and resource, digital, psychological-pedagogical, and monitoring and evaluation components. The scientific novelty of the study lies in the systematic structuring of the challenges facing STEM education in Ukrainian pedagogical higher education institutions under wartime conditions, the identification of their interrelationships, and the conceptualization of STEM teacher education as an adaptive, resilient, and digitally oriented system. The novelty also consists in substantiating a model of its functioning that integrates enabling, process-oriented, and outcome-oriented components. The practical significance of the study lies in the potential application of its findings to the modernization of educational and professional programs for prospective STEM teachers, the development of institutional STEM education strategies in pedagogical universities, the planning and renewal of digital and laboratory infrastructure, the professional development of academic and teaching staff, the expansion of international partnerships, and the implementation of innovative educational technologies. The study concludes that the effective functioning of STEM education in Ukrainian pedagogical higher education institutions under wartime conditions requires a transition from fragmented responses to individual challenges towards a systemic and adaptive model focused on educational resilience, digital transformation, human-resource development, institutional and resource capacity, and the quality of professional preparation of prospective teachers. Such an approach provides a conceptual foundation for the modernization and sustainable development of pedagogical STEM education during both the wartime and post-war periods.

title: ReInVenTa: UNIVERSIDAD INTELIGENTE PARA LA INCLUSIÓN SOCIOECONÓMICA Y LA TRANSFORMACIÓN DEL MERCADO LABORAL EN LA REGIÓN HUETAR NORTE
summary: La transformación digital y la expansión de la inteligencia artificial están generando cambios acelerados en los modelos productivos y en las dinámicas del mercado laboral, planteando nuevos desafíos para la formación universitaria. En la Región Huetar Norte de Costa Rica, caracterizada por una estructura productiva diversa, resulta necesario fortalecer la articulación entre la academia, el sector empresarial y la sociedad mediante información sistematizada sobre las demandas de talento y las competencias requeridas. En este contexto, ReInVenTa (Red de Inteligencia y Vinculación en Talento) se desarrolla como una plataforma digital que integra análisis de datos y monitoreo en línea para generar información sobre vacantes, empleadores y competencias demandadas, orientada a la toma de decisiones académicas. Este artículo presenta los resultados de la primera fase del proyecto, a partir de una muestra de 541 personas egresadas de 13 carreras universitarias. Los resultados permiten identificar patrones de inserción laboral, principales sectores empleadores, competencias desarrolladas y brechas entre la oferta de talento y las demandas del mercado laboral. Asimismo, se presenta el diseño metodológico de las fases posteriores, orientadas al análisis de empleadores y a la lectura automatizada de vacantes. Los hallazgos evidencian la utilidad del modelo para identificar desajustes de competencias (skills mismatch) y aportar información para la toma de decisiones académicas basada en datos, con potencial para contribuir al fortalecimiento de la empleabilidad y la transformación del mercado laboral regional. Palabras clave: inteligencia artificial, transformación digital, mercado laboral, empleabilidad, brecha de competencias Abstract Digital transformation and the expansion of artificial intelligence are generating rapid changes in production models and labor market dynamics, posing new challenges for university education. In Costa Rica’s Huetar Norte Region, characterized by a diverse productive structure, it is necessary to strengthen coordination among academia, the business sector, and society through systematic information on talent demands and the competencies required. In this context, ReInVenTa (Intelligence and Talent Linkage Network) is being developed as a digital platform that integrates data analysis and online monitoring to generate information on job vacancies, employers, and required competencies, supporting academic decision-making. This article presents the results of the first phase of the project, based on a sample of 541 graduates from 13 university programs. The results identify employment integration patterns, main employing sectors, competencies developed, and gaps between the supply of talent and labor market demands. The article also presents the methodological design of subsequent phases, aimed at analyzing employers and conducting automated job vacancy analysis. The findings demonstrate the usefulness of the model for identifying skills mismatches and providing data-driven information to support academic decision-making, with the potential to contribute to strengthening employability and transforming the regional labor market. title: Steering for Safety, Hijacking for Profit: Trojan Threats in the LLM Activation Steering Supply Chain
summary: As large language models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into Web search, online recommendation, and intelligent decision-making, the third-party plugin ecosystem centered on model customization continues to grow. Among these, Steering Vectors guide model behavior by intervening in internal representations. However, the open plugin ecosystem also introduces new supply-chain security risks: malicious plugins can disguise themselves as having legitimate functionality and covertly manipulate outputs without significantly affecting model performance. Although this risk poses a real threat, the security issues of Steering plugins in the LLM supply-chain ecosystem still lack systematic research. This paper audits eight mainstream open-source Steering plugin libraries and reveals three structural vulnerabilities: insufficient distribution integrity verification, excessive plugin privileges, and missing runtime monitoring, which offers an attack surface for attackers. To investigate this threat, we propose a malicious plugin, IDH. Specifically, IDH designs a norm-gated mutually exclusive routing mechanism and proposes an information-decay inflection point localization method to automatically select the injection layer, thereby simultaneously achieving benign and malicious functions. To counter such threats, we propose a runtime defense framework, by suppressing anomalous activation interventions and orthogonalizing inter-layer trajectory. We evaluate IDH across five mainstream LLMs, using safety-refusal steering as the legitimate functionality and commercial recommendation manipulation as the hijack objective. Experiments covering six brands across three commercial domains demonstrate that IDH achieves an attack success rate (ASR) of up to 97.8% while preserving high refusal rates on harmful requests.

title: Artificial intelligence's effect on financial reports for listed banks in Saudi Arabia
summary: Objectives: This study investigated the impact of artificial intelligence (AI) on financial accounting practices in banks listed on the Saudi Stock Exchange (Tadawul), focusing on system integration, reporting accuracy, information interpretation, and presentation quality within a survey-based empirical context. It also considered the perceived benefits and challenges of AI adoption in the Saudi banking sector. Method: The study employed a quantitative, survey-based design, using primary data collected through a structured questionnaire administered to accountants, auditors, financial analysts, and managers in Saudi banks. Data were analyzed using SPSS, and reliability testing showed strong internal consistency, with Cronbach’s alpha values ranging from 0.889 to 0.931. Results: The findings indicated statistically significant positive associations between AI adoption and all examined dimensions of financial accounting practices, with correlation coefficients ranging from 0.54 to 0.87 (p <.01). Conclusion: The study provided empirical evidence from a survey-based investigation indicating that AI adoption was associated with improvements in the quality and efficiency of financial reporting in Saudi banks. These results reflected perceived relationships rather than causal effects, contributing to the limited literature on AI in financial accounting in emerging markets and offering practical implications for policymakers and banking leaders.

title: Geopolitical forces and strategic decision-making in multinational firms: a scorecard and heatmap comparative analysis
summary: In an increasingly interconnected world, the knowledge economy-encompassing technology, education and research-faces complex challenges posed by the evolving geopolitical dynamics. This paper examines how multinational companies strategically respond to these shifts. Through a compre­hensive analysis of regulatory changes, political instability, trade policies and decarbonization concerns, this paper highlights the composite nature of geopolitical risks and their influence on corporate strate­gy. Methodologically, the research employs a scorecard and a heatmap to provide a systematic, organ­ization‑level framework for comparing firms’ strategic responses. The scorecard evaluates regulatory compliance, supply chain resilience, risk management, strategic partnerships, innovation and carbon reduction targets across Apple, SAP and Tesla, with scores ranging from 2.00 to 4.00. Apple achieves the highest overall score (3.33/4), followed by Tesla (3.00/4) and SAP (2.83/4), indicating differences in inno­vation, policy alignment and supply chain resilience. The heatmap compares TotalEnergies, Danfoss and General Electric across eight decarbonization indicators, showing Danfoss as the sustainability leader. General Electric exhibits strong renewable‑energy capabilities, but remains constrained by legacy infra­structure. By applying this comparative framework, the study identifies improvement areas and offers strategic recommendations to help multinational companies strengthen geopolitical risk management and maintain competitive advantage in a rapidly changing global environment.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Digital Transformation in the National Environmental Standards and Regulations Enforcement Agency, 2014-2026
summary: Artificial Intelligence (AI) and digital transformation have increasingly become important instruments for improving efficiency, transparency, accountability, decision-making, and service delivery in public organisations. This study examined Artificial Intelligence and digital transformation in the National Environmental Standards and Regulations Enforcement Agency (NESREA) from 2014 to 2026. Specifically, the study sought to examine the influence of machine learning on bureaucratic imperatives and the influence of digital data management systems on decision-making. The study adopted the survey research design and used primary and secondary data. The population of the study comprises 300 officials from which 171 respondents were determined using Taro Yamane’s formula and purposively selected. Structured questionnaire were administered to elicit information from the 160 retrieved questionnaire which was subsequently analysed, representing a 93.6% retrieval rate. The research instrument was validated by experts, while reliability was determined using Cronbach’s Alpha. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics and Pearson Product-Moment Correlation in SPSS. Findings showed that machine learning improved on administrative imperatives, with a grand mean of 2.98 and a positive relationship with bureaucratic efficiency at; r = 0.684, p = 0.000. Digital data management systems enhanced decision-making at; grand mean = 3.04; r = 0.721, p = 0.000. The study concluded that digital technologies significantly strengthened administrative performance in NESREA. The study thus, recommended that NESREA should adopt stronger machine learning, and improved digital data infrastructure, as well as staff capacity development, and technical support in other to improve and sustain NESREA environmental governance capacity.

title: Accounting Treatment of BPJS Health Insurance Claims Using PSAK 74 Principles at PKU Wonosobo
summary: BPJS Kesehatan claims constitute a major source of revenue for PKU Muhammadiyah Wonosobo Hospital. However, claim submission, verification through the Berita Acara Hasil Verifikasi (BAHV), and post-audit adjustments may affect the value of receivables reported at the end of the accounting period. This study examines the recognition, measurement, presentation, and disclosure of revenue from BPJS Kesehatan claims, using the principles of PSAK 74 as an analytical benchmark rather than an accounting standard directly applicable to the hospital. A descriptive-comparative qualitative approach was employed. Data were collected from finance staff and the finance manager through unstructured interviews, observations of financial reporting practices, and a review of claim submission documents, BAHV records, accounting policies, and journal entries. A detailed examination of the January 2026 service period was conducted within the broader context of financial reporting for 2024–2025. The findings indicate that the hospital recognizes revenue on an accrual basis upon completion of healthcare services, initially measures claims based on applicable hospital tariffs and Indonesian Case-Based Groups (INA-CBGs) reimbursement rates, and subsequently adjusts receivables according to claim submission, verification, and audit outcomes. BPJS Kesehatan receivables are presented as a single current asset account without systematic classification by claim aging or verification status, while disclosures concerning claim-related uncertainties remain limited and general. The findings suggest that the principles of PSAK 74 can provide a useful comparative framework for strengthening risk-based receivables classification and financial statement disclosures.

title: From PingAn’s Inspiration to HDFC ERGO’s Journey: Building an Insurance-Based Ecosystem
summary: Beginning with an exploration of insurance player Ping An’s evolution to contrast with HDFC ERGO’s strategy adaptation to the Indian market, this case sheds light on HDFC ERGO’s strategic shift towards a mindshare-centric ecosystem from its roots as a digitised insurance provider in India.The case starts with Ping An, which is perhaps the best-known successful example of an insurance-based multi-product (and multi-actor) ecosystem. It looks at Ping An’s journey, emphasising its digital transformation, ecosystem expansions and technology integration. It then turns to HDFC ERGO, which aimed to create its own ecosystem, and considers the similarities and differences. Drawing parallels and contrasts with India’s burgeoning startup ecosystem and the transformative India Stack, HDFC ERGO crafted unique strategic principles. It emphasised avoiding direct competition, offering tangential value, filling market voids and balancing mindshare with value. Utilising internal capabilities and market insights, HDFC ERGO focused on healthcare, leveraging data and digital infrastructure. The development of the ‘Here’ app exemplifies the company’s strategic prowess, aligning healthcare solutions with customer preferences.The case illuminates HDFC ERGO’s meticulous approach to tailoring an ecosystem strategy amid shifting market dynamics and technological landscapes, and shows how it built its multi-actor ecosystem in various verticals to support its multi-product ecosystem play. It showcases the company’s adeptness in adapting strategies while embracing innovation, resonating with market needs to forge a unique path in the evolving digital insurance realm.This case study stands on its own, offering valuable lessons on strategic planning and execution in the rapidly evolving digital and consumer landscapes. However, when taught in conjunction with its sister case “HDFC ERGO: A product ecosystem built on mindshare” (LBS CS-24-009), students can gain a comprehensive understanding of both the macro-strategic vision and the micro-level steps that underpin HDFC ERGO’s ecosystem approach. title: Designing a Gamified Tool: An ADDIE Approach to Capital Market Flashcard Development
summary: Traditional, lecture-based finance courses frequently overwhelm undergraduate students with dense theoretical content, leading to poor knowledge retention, lower overall engagement, and a heavy reliance on last-minute cramming before major assessments. To address these persistent educational challenges, this study details the design, development, and implementation of a mobile-friendly digital flashcard game specifically tailored for an undergraduate Financial Markets and Institutions (FIN) course using the systematic ADDIE instructional design framework. By integrating active recall strategies, custom visual aids, and an algorithm-driven Spaced Repetition System (SRS), the platform transforms passive studying into a dynamic learning process that prompts students to systematically review challenging concepts based on their individual mastery levels. Subject-matter experts rigorously vetted the curriculum content for accuracy and practical relevance prior to deployment, while formative evaluations directly measured student usability, overall engagement, and conceptual comprehension during active coursework. Formative findings, including high expert ratings for content validity and evidence of adaptive scheduling from system logs, suggest that the tool has strong potential to support active recall. However, its effectiveness in improving long-term knowledge retention and reducing academic anxiety will be examined in a subsequent summative evaluation. Ultimately, by documenting the comprehensive analysis, design, and development phases, this study provides instructional designers and finance educators with a practical, replicable blueprint for implementing gamified, technology-enhanced active learning tools across complex capital markets curricula.

title: Do PCAOB Inspection Deficiencies Related to Management Review Controls Affect Financial Reporting Decisions? Evidence From Goodwill Impairments
summary: ABSTRACT We examine whether PCAOB inspection deficiencies related to management review controls (MRCs) affect financial reporting decisions. Using the goodwill impairment setting, we find that firms are more likely to record goodwill impairments when their auditors have received more PCAOB inspection deficiencies related to goodwill MRCs. The association is stronger when inspection deficiencies are more likely to lead to changes to the design or implementation of an internal control (repeat deficiencies and deficiencies related to MRC precision). We observe some evidence that MRC inspection deficiencies increase the likelihood of goodwill impairment even when unrelated to goodwill, indicating that improving the audit of MRCs can broadly affect financial reporting. Our findings provide evidence that PCAOB inspections affect not only auditor behavior but also the financial reporting behavior of audit clients. Specifically, inspection feedback appears to influence reporting outcomes through changes in the audit and evaluation of MRCs, identifying a channel through which regulatory oversight affects issuers. The results have implications for audit firms seeking to remediate inspection deficiencies, for management and audit committees responsible for overseeing significant estimates and impairment analyses, and for regulators evaluating the broader effectiveness of the PCAOB inspection process.

title: Mobile Edge AI Framework for Real-Time ESG Compliance Auditing through NLP and Blockchain Ledger Verification
summary: The Mobile Edge artificial intelligence (AI) framework is introduced as an environmental, social, and governance (ESG) verification system that integrates natural language processing (NLP) and permissioned blockchain to facilitate near-real-time ESG compliance auditing. A lightweight transformer model is employed to identify ESG-related claims and extract relevant indicators, numerical values, units, locations, and reporting times. Extracted claims are structured and recorded on the blockchain to ensure verifiable, tamper-resistant records. A discrepancy assessment mechanism then classifies each claim as supported, partially supported, contradictory, or unsupported. The prototype was evaluated using a synthetic Kaggle dataset containing 11,000 annual company records from 1,000 organizations across nine regions and multiple sectors. The ESG classification model achieved a true positive rate of approximately 93.2%, with F1-scores of 0.945, 0.915, and 0.895 for environmental, social, and governance claims, respectively. Claim verification rates ranged from 93.1% to 98.4%. Edge deployment reduced verification latency to 124 ms compared to 231 ms in the cloud environment, representing a 46.3% reduction. These findings indicate that the framework can enable proactive ESG auditing, enhance claim traceability, accelerate verification, and deliver explainable compliance-risk signals.

title: The Legacy of Indecision: Why Family Wealth Survives Generations but Decisions Do Not
summary: The Legacy of Indecision Why Family Wealth Survives Generations but Decisions Do Not Abstract Family wealth may endure across generations while the capacity to make and activate consequential decisions becomes increasingly fragile. Financial continuity does not necessarily ensure continuity in leadership, accountability or governance. This conceptual research paper examines why business families and family-owned enterprises may preserve substantial assets while leaving critical questions of succession, ownership, control and strategic renewal unresolved. Drawing on Decision Non-Closure (DNC), originated by Dr Birgit Maria Kemphues, the paper distinguishes three stages of organisational decision-making: formal decision approval, accountable activation and implementation performance. The analysis considers financial, social, emotional, intellectual and values-based capital as interconnected dimensions of family continuity. It explores how intergenerational expectations, family loyalty, ambiguous authority and competing priorities may contribute to persistent decision non-closure. Four conceptual research propositions examine the relationship between ownership structures, governance arrangements, succession and decision activation. A governance matrix and a hypothetical succession scenario illustrate how apparent agreement may coexist with unresolved responsibilities and delayed implementation. The paper extends the DNC framework to family wealth governance and intergenerational decision-making, contributing a conceptual perspective to the Decision Non-Closure Research Programme (DNC-RP) within International Boardroom Studies. The study is theoretical and conceptual. It does not present original empirical findings or claim that its propositions have been empirically validated. Research Contribution The central contribution of this paper is the distinction between the preservation of family wealth and the preservation of a family's capacity to make binding decisions. It proposes that continuity of ownership and continuity of decision-making authority should not be treated as equivalent. By applying Decision Non-Closure to intergenerational governance, the paper offers a framework for examining situations in which succession plans, strategic agreements or family governance arrangements appear settled but remain operationally incomplete. The framework identifies three conditions relevant to accountable decision activation: An identifiable person or body responsible for the decision. A clearly defined first implementation action. A documented mechanism for review and follow-up. These conditions are proposed as conceptual indicators, not as an empirically validated measurement instrument. About the Author Dr Birgit Maria Kemphues studies the decisions that organisations believe they have already made. She is an Independent Researcher and Author, the originator of Decision Non-Closure (DNC), and Research Director of the Decision Non-Closure Research Programme (DNC-RP) within International Boardroom Studies. Her independent research began in 2010. Since 2020, her work has focused particularly on international decision-making, cross-cultural leadership and corporate governance. In 2025, she established the DNC Research Programme. Her research draws on more than 35 years of experience across over 400 projects in Europe, the Gulf region and Asia. Internationally, she is also known as The Boardroom Emergency Doctor. title: Institutional Corruption, ESG, and Corporate Tax Behavior: Evidence from MENA Economies
summary: Weak institutional environments may encourage aggressive corporate tax practices, but firms’ responses can vary depending on the strength of their internal governance. This study examines the relationship between perceived corruption risk and corporate tax avoidance and investigates whether firm-level environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance moderates this relationship. Using an unbalanced panel of 921 publicly listed firms, comprising 7628 firm-year observations across 11 Middle East and North Africa (MENA) economies from 2013 to 2024, the study employs fixed-effects panel regressions alongside several robustness checks. The findings indicate that greater perceived corruption risk is associated with higher corporate tax avoidance, while stronger ESG performance significantly weakens this association. Subsample analyses also reveal positive CORRISK × ESG interaction coefficients in both higher- and lower-corruption economies, with a larger estimated coefficient in the higher-corruption group. The main findings remain broadly consistent when using an alternative measure of tax avoidance, two-step System GMM, additional firm- and country-level controls, and alternative fixed-effects specifications. However, the country-level corruption measure reflects the broader institutional environment rather than firms’ direct exposure to corruption, which should be considered when interpreting the results. Overall, the study highlights the potential role of firm-level ESG in mitigating the relationship between perceived corruption risk and aggressive corporate tax behavior, emphasizing the importance of considering both institutional conditions and corporate governance practices in MENA economies.

title: PEDAGOGICAL POTENTIAL OF BENCHMARKING IN THE CONDITIONS OF DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION OF EDUCATION
summary: Relevance of the Study. The article is devoted to highlighting the problem of pedagogical potential of benchmarking in the conditions of digital transformation of education. The relevance of the research is determined by the need to find effective mechanisms for ensuring the quality of education in the conditions of active implementation of digital technologies and the formation of the digital educational space of higher education institutions. It has been established that the digitalization of education contributes to the modernization of the content, forms and methods of education, the expansion of access to educational resources, the development of digital competences and the improvement of educational communication. The purpose of the article was to substantiate the pedagogical potential of benchmarking in the conditions of digital transformation of education, to reveal the peculiarities of the implementation of the benchmarking approach to increasing the efficiency and quality of the educational process. To achieve this goal, methods of analysis, synthesis, generalisation, and systematisation of scientific sources were employed. Research Methods. The study employed theoretical methods, including analysis, synthesis, generalisation, and systematisation of scholarly and regulatory sources on educational digitalisation, digital transformation, quality assurance, and benchmarking. Comparative analysis was used to examine international experience and to identify opportunities and barriers related to digital benchmarking in education. Results. Benchmarking was defined as a systematic process of searching for, analysing, comparing, and adapting effective educational practices. The analysis showed that digital platforms, cloud services, open educational resources, electronic databases, and professional networks expand opportunities to compare educational practices, disseminate innovation, support teachers' professional development, and improve educational content and organisation. The study also identified implementation barriers in Ukraine, including uneven digital infrastructure, limited resources, insufficient awareness of benchmarking methodology, and the absence of systematic mechanisms for sharing effective practices. Conclusions. Benchmarking has considerable pedagogical potential as a quality improvement tool in a digitally transformed educational environment. Its effective use requires critical adaptation rather than mechanical transfer of external practices. Further development should focus on methodological guidance, evaluation criteria, professional educational networks, international cooperation, and national mechanisms for disseminating effective educational practices

title: ADAPTING UK AND EU CORPORATE GOVERNANCE MODELS TO NIGERIA: A ROADMAP FOR M&A SUCCESS
summary: The proposed expansion of cross-border mergers and acquisitions (M&As) within the Nigerian banking sector has remained hampered by structural weaknesses in the domestic corporate governance framework, undermining both the stability and longevity of these transactions. Despite the global ubiquity of governance challenges, issues specific to the Nigerian ecosystem, ranging from constrained board independence to weak shareholder protection and opaque regulatory oversight, necessitate a robust, comprehensive, and context-relatable framework capable of navigating complex M&A dynamics. The authors evaluated sustainable solutions to these governance deficits by assessing the adaptability of corporate governance models from the United Kingdom (UK) and the European Union (EU), jurisdictions, apparently selected premised on the fact that Nigeria’s corporate law regime, is rooted in English common law and because both systems represent internationally recognised benchmarks of governance regulation. The paper maintained that a critical analysis of key statutory instruments, including the UK Corporate Governance Code, the UK Takeover Code, and the EU Shareholder Rights Directive, is in tandem with Nigeria’s Companies and Allied Matters Act 2020, the Banks and Other Financial Institutions Act 2020, the Central Bank of Nigeria Corporate Governance Guidelines 2023, and the Nigerian Code of Corporate Governance.

title: LA INTELIGENCIA ARTIFICIAL EN LA INNOVACIÓN EMPRESARIAL: APLICACIÓN DE LA GAMIFICACIÓN EN LA FORMACIÓN CORPORATIVA, ESTUDIO DE CASO
summary: La transformación digital plantea nuevas exigencias para la formación del capital humano corporativo y evidencia limitaciones en las estrategias tradicionales de capacitación frente a las necesidades de aprendizaje ágil, colaborativo y personalizado del entorno empresarial contemporáneo. En este contexto, la convergencia entre inteligencia artificial (IA) y gamificación constituye una alternativa innovadora para fortalecer los procesos de formación. El presente estudio analiza el impacto de la IA en la innovación de procesos, con énfasis en la aplicación de la gamificación y las experiencias inmersivas como estrategias para la capacitación y la optimización del aprendizaje. Se presenta un estudio de caso aplicado a una entidad financiera de Quito, Ecuador, mediante un serious game orientado al fortalecimiento de la cultura organizacional a través de dinámicas colaborativas. Se empleó un enfoque metodológico mixto, basado en entrevistas semiestructuradas, análisis documental, observación de entornos y pruebas de aplicabilidad. Los resultados evidencian un alto nivel de acceso técnico y usabilidad inicial, dado que la mayoría de los participantes logró acceder, instalar e interactuar con la aplicación sin inconvenientes significativos. No obstante, se identificó una brecha entre la autopercepción de los participantes y su desempeño real durante la dinámica del juego. Se concluye que, aunque la gamificación apoyada por IA presenta viabilidad técnica, requiere mejoras en el diseño comunicacional y pedagógico para favorecer la comprensión de los roles y la colaboración efectiva. El estudio aporta evidencia sobre esta brecha y orientaciones para el diseño de serious games aplicados a la formación corporativa. Para explicar la brecha identificada, se proponen tres métricas exploratorias: Perception–Performance Gap (PPG), Behavioral Calibration Ratio (BCR) y Technical–Pedagogical Drop (TPD). Palabra clave: gamificación, innovación tecnológica, inteligencia artificial, negocios Abstract Digital transformation poses new demands on corporate human capital development and highlights limitations in traditional training strategies in addressing the need for agile, collaborative, and personalized learning in the contemporary business environment. In this context, the convergence of artificial intelligence (AI) and gamification represents an innovative alternative for strengthening training processes. This study analyzes the impact of AI on process innovation, with an emphasis on the application of gamification and immersive experiences as strategies for training and learning optimization. A case study was conducted in a financial institution in Quito, Ecuador, using a serious game aimed at strengthening organizational culture through collaborative dynamics. A mixed-methods approach was employed, based on semi-structured interviews, document analysis, environmental observation, and applicability testing. The results indicate a high level of initial technical access and usability, as most participants were able to access, install, and interact with the application without significant difficulties. However, a gap was identified between participants’ self-perception and their actual performance during the game dynamics. The study concludes that, although AI-supported gamification demonstrates technical feasibility, improvements in communicational and pedagogical design are required to promote role comprehension and effective collaboration. The study provides evidence of this gap and offers guidelines for the design of serious games applied to corporate training. To explain the identified gap, three exploratory metrics are proposed: Perception–Performance Gap (PPG), Behavioral Calibration Ratio (BCR), and Technical–Pedagogical Drop (TPD). title: Peculiarities of accounting policy formation at unitary enterprises
summary: The relevance of the research topic is due to the need to study the specifics of the formation of accounting policies of unitary enterprises in the context of constant changes in legislation and increased requirements for transparency of financial reporting. A well-formed accounting policy makes it possible to ensure the reliability of accounting information, increase the efficiency of enterprise management and minimize financial risks. The work is based on the study of international financial reporting standards and federal accounting standards, scientific works of leading Russian and foreign scientists in the field under study. The research uses methods of analysis and synthesis, expert assessments and logical generalization. The purpose of this work is to consider the specifics of the accounting policy of unitary enterprises, identify the main problems of its formation and analyze the specifics of accounting in these organizations.

title: China Evergrande Group's High-Leverage Capital Structure: Formation Logic and Risk Evolution from a Corporate Finance Perspective
summary: The real estate sector is by nature capital-intensive, and high leverage has long been a standard practice for property developers across global markets. In China, the debt-fueled high-turnover growth model has backed the rapid expansion of the property industry for decades, but it has also built up considerable hidden debt risks. The launch of the "Three Red Lines" regulatory policy in 2020 has sharply tightened financing rules for developers, and the risks tied to extreme leverage strategies have gradually come to the surface. As the most representative player with an aggressive leverage strategy in the industry, China Evergrande Group's 2021 debt default has become a landmark case of corporate financial distress. This paper uses a literature review combined with case study analysis, and draws on trade-off theory and financial distress cost frameworks, supplemented by an accounting perspective, to explain how Evergrande's high-leverage capital structure formed and how its risks evolved and spread. The study finds that Evergrande's leverage level moved far past the optimal range predicted by traditional theory, pushed by scale expansion incentives, implicit expectations of policy support, and internal managerial agency problems. Accounting tools such as off-balance-sheet financing further hid the true size of its debt burden. Once external financing conditions tightened, accumulated risks set off a spiral of rising financial distress costs, which eventually grew into a full-scale liquidity crisis.

title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Improving Accounting and Auditing Practices: A Study of Selected Organizations in Uganda
summary: This systematic literature review (SLR) synthesises evidence on how artificial intelligence (AI) is improving accounting and auditing practice, with specific attention to selected organizations in Uganda: audit and accountancy firms, public-sector accounting entities, small and medium-sized practices, and the professional body. The review followed PRISMA 2020 and an a priori protocol. Peer-reviewed and professional-body sources published from 2015 onward were identified through multi-database searching and citation chasing, screened against explicit criteria, appraised with the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT) and an adapted checklist for conceptual papers, and analysed through thematic synthesis. Nineteen studies were included. This systematic literature review found that: (1) documented applications and benefits; (2) low and uneven adoption, especially in Uganda; (3) technology, organizational and environmental determinants of adoption; (4) skills, education and workforce effects; and (5) ethics, governance and regulation. Ugandan evidence is limited to one survey of professional accountants and one conference study of public-sector readiness; no study measured audit-quality or cost outcomes of AI in a Ugandan organization. Most evidence relies on perception data from single-country cross-sections. Implications: Regulators, firms and educators should prioritise skills, governance and affordable tooling; researchers should pursue organization-level, longitudinal and outcome-based designs. Originality: To our knowledge, this is the first SLR focused on AI in accounting and auditing in Uganda.

title: A cross-cycle water-accounting vulnerability in NHANES: a paired audit of a published mortality exposure
summary: Background. Zhou et al. (2022) reported inverse associations of dietary water-source intake with mortality in 35,463 NHANES participants from 1999–2014. Beginning in 2005–2006, NHANES recorded plain drinking water as itemised intake and included it in total dietary moisture. We examined whether a literal implementation of the published exposure definitions could add this water twice. Methods. We compared CDC dietary-total and item-level records across eight NHANES cycles and constructed two source-water definitions in the same screened sample (N = 35,163). One followed a potentially duplicative literal residual; the other removed post-2005 plain water from the residual exactly once. We examined cycle discontinuities, distributional proximity to Zhou et al.'s published summary, and quartile reassignment. Exploratory mortality analyses used a distinct, non-equivalent Cox model with NCHS public-use follow-up through 2019. New robustness analyses refitted the archived model after restricting survey cycles to 2003–2014, with and without requiring a valid second-day recall. Results. The original article's exposure definitions imply the potentially duplicative M + P construction unless an unreported harmonisation step was used. In 101,153 matched person-days, item-moisture sums reconciled with the reported aggregate to numerical precision. The literal versus corrected definitions yielded paired-sample median food-water residuals of 949 versus 556 g/day; the published Zhou median was 924 g/day. The vulnerable reconstruction created a post-2005 jump in median apparent food-water share from approximately 21% to 41–46%; the non-duplicative calculation remained approximately 20–25%. In the pooled exploratory 2019 model (31,046 participants; 5,898 deaths), the Q4/Q1 hazard ratios were 0.910 (95% CI 0.805–1.029) and 0.979 (0.883–1.085). In the 2003–2014 restricted cohort they were 0.984 and 1.014; with only valid second-day recalls, 1.026 and 1.046. All corresponding intervals included 1. A complete 48-row archive of exploratory model fits also includes materially different specifications, and cannot support a stable mortality-effect claim. Conclusions. The literal post-2005 accounting vulnerability and large exposure-classification differences are demonstrable. Similarity of a vulnerable reconstruction to published marginal distributions raises a specific implementation concern, but Zhou et al.'s actual code is unavailable; we cannot establish that the original authors made that error. The mortality-model difference in our audit is exploratory and sensitive to survey-era and recall-completeness choices; it is not a corrected estimate of the original published association.

title: The Impact of Local Government ESG Performance on Foreign Direct Investment
summary: In the complex and ever-changing international economic environment, stabilizing existing foreign investment and promoting new inflows are key priorities for government administrations. The sustainable development philosophy embodied in ESG (Environment, Social Responsibility and Governance) practices provides entities with sufficient competitiveness and attracts the attention of international investors. Using panel data of 31 provinces in China from 2015 to 2020, this study employs a two-way fixed-effects model to examine the impact of local government ESG performance on FDI (foreign direct investment). The results indicate that good ESG performance significantly enhances foreign investment inflows and the mechanism test confirmed that optimizing the business environment and improving total factor productivity are crucial channels through which ESG practices attract foreign investment. Further analysis revealed that the positive effect of ESG performance on stabilizing foreign investment is more pronounced in regions with low resource dependence, and a developed digital economy environment amplifies the positive impact of ESG activities on foreign investment. However, ESG practices widen the FDI gap across regions, exhibiting a distinct “Matthew effect”. Consequently, this paper proposes several policy recommendations, such as improving local government ESG information disclosure and evaluation systems, enhancing ESG performance to create locational advantages, and formulating strategic plans tailored to local conditions.
