title: The Impact of the Rural Digital Economy on Ecological Product Value Conversion Efficiency from the Perspective of Production–Living–Ecological Functions
summary: The rapid expansion of the rural digital economy (RDE) has introduced new opportunities for enhancing ecological product value conversion efficiency (EPVCE), yet the mechanisms underlying this relationship remain insufficiently understood. Based on provincial panel data from 31 Chinese provinces during 2010–2019, this study constructs an RDE index system and evaluates EPVCE using a super-efficiency slack-based measure (SBM) model. Two-way fixed-effects models, bootstrap mediation analysis, heterogeneity tests, and spatial Durbin models are employed to examine the impact of RDE on EPVCE and explore the underlying mechanisms. The findings reveal that (1) RDE is significantly and positively associated with EPVCE, and this finding remains robust to alternative model specifications and variable measures, controls for climatic factors, a one-period lag of RDE, and an instrumental-variable approach; (2) production, living, and ecological functions constitute key transmission channels, with the ecological function exhibiting a relatively larger indirect effect; (3) the positive relationship is more pronounced in eastern China and non-resource-based provinces, indicating substantial heterogeneity; and (4) spatial analysis reveals that the relationship is primarily characterized by local effects rather than spatial spillovers. From a rural multifunctionality perspective, this study extends research on the RDE–EPVCE nexus and provides empirical evidence for coordinating rural digital transformation with ecological value realization.

title: Where to Site Direct Air Capture? Optimal Global Supply Chains from Capture to Storage
summary: The cost and net removal efficiency of direct air capture with CO2 storage (DACCS) depend strongly on siting, power supply, and how captured CO2 reaches storage. Here, we present a globally resolved (1° × 1°) assessment of solid-sorbent DACCS supply chains for near-term and mid-century scenarios, coupling hourly techno-economic optimization, (prospective) life-cycle assessment, and multimodal CO2 transport to storage to estimate net levelized costs of carbon dioxide removal that account for cradle-to-grave greenhouse gas emissions. In the near-term, the cheapest sites require ∼1,100–1,200 USD/tCO2 in the central United States and western Australia; cost is governed less by CO2 capture than by access to CO2 transport and storage and the regional cost of capital, while local wind resources enable the cheapest sites. A siting hierarchy emerges: proximity to geological storage is preferred, and a well-connected port is a near-equivalent substitute where storage is distant. By 2050, a lower-carbon global economy, cheaper CO2 transport, and technological learning broaden low-cost deployment, with ∼98% of sites below 1,000 USD/tCO2 (cheapest ∼370) at a median ∼93% removal efficiency. Near-term first-mover regions remain the lowest in cost, indicating low risk of stranded assets.

summary: The article examines the process of digital transformation of fundraising in non-profit and cultural organizations at the current stage of development in Russia and abroad. The authors survey the theoretical foundations of digital fundraising, highlight its main digital tools (social networks, crowdfunding platforms, CRM systems, PR campaigns, email marketing). The paper also presents a comprehensive model of digital fundraising, which includes a methodology for setting goals (SMART), strategic analysis (SWOT), and a system of efficacy evaluation indicators (KPI, ROI, NPS). The statistical data analysis of the crowdfunding platform Planeta.ru is performed and the main trends in the development of digital fundraising in Russia are identified. The research results demonstrate that the integration of traditional fundraising mechanisms with digital tools contributes to the sustainable development of cultural organizations in the culture field. It is concluded that the last needs a modernization at the expense of the skilled workers renewal, the uprise of their digital competence, electronic platforms distribution in the regional institutes, and the adoption of the experience of financing them by the effect of multiple stakeholders.

title: Does ESG really create value? Evidence from profitability, dividend policy, and CSR in Islamic banking
summary: Purpose This study aims to analyze the influence of profitability, corporate social responsibility (CSR) and dividend policy on the value of Sharia Bank companies with Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) performance as a mediation variable. Design/methodology/approach The method used in this study is Structural Equation Modeling with Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) multiple linear regression. The data used were obtained from the company’s annual report, selected through purposive sampling. Findings The analysis indicates that profitability and dividend policy have a positive, statistically significant impact on the company’s value. However, profitability can undermine ESG considerations, whereas a dividend policy can enhance ESG. Additionally, ESG has been shown to have a positive, significant effect on a company’s value. Another important finding is that ESG plays a significant mediating role in the relationship between profitability and dividend policy on company value. This suggests that the greater a company’s attention to ESG factors, the greater the impact on its value. Research limitations/implications This research suggests that companies must strike a balance between financial performance and sustainability commitments to create more optimal long-term value. ESG can be a crucial strategy for building a reputation and enhancing investor confidence. Originality/value The researchers used a more representative sample of 12 Islamic banks in Indonesia, given the industry’s diverse characteristics and regulations. Research that specifically examines the role of ESG as a mediating variable in Islamic banking. The researcher examines how dividend policies affect the ESG performance of Islamic banks, given the importance of social and environmental factors in their operations. Researchers used more complex statistical methods, such as OLS in SPSS or panel data analysis, to analyze the relationships between variables in more depth. With this, it is hoped that a more comprehensive understanding of the factors that affect the value of Islamic bank companies, as well as the role of ESG in this context, can be obtained.

title: Towards an integrated framework for digital transformation in Moroccan higher education
summary: Digital transformation of public universities in developing countries raises a number of difficulties that relate to their institutions' characteristics and strategies. In Morocco, these challenges are amplified by structural, organizational, and technological limitations that hinder the deployment of comprehensive digital initiatives. Despite the presence of a wide range of DX Frameworks in literature, very few are adapted to the specific context of higher education institutions. This study follows a Design Science Research approach combining a systematic literature review with structured expert validation. The systematic literature review investigates how existing DX frameworks integrate critical success factors and to what extent they address the complex, multidimensional nature of transformation in higher education. Through this review, we selected and analyzed 22 relevant frameworks covering various sectors. This analysis reveals that most existing frameworks emphasize technology and strategy but often overlook essential dimensions such as change management, governance, evaluation or data integration. Based on these insights, we propose a holistic DX framework for Moroccan Public Universities (MPU). We structured our framework around seven interdependent dimensions: strategy & Governance, Organization & Processes, Technologies & Infrastructures, Human Capital & Organizational Culture & Change management, Pedagogy & Research, and Data & Evaluation & Continuous improvement. Each dimension is supported by sub-dimensions and interrelations that guide institutions through a structured and adaptive transformation process. We submitted the proposed framework to expert validation through the Content Validity Index (CVI) methodology, involving a panel of 22 domain Experts. Results confirmed strong content validity, with an overall S-CVI/Ave of 0.88 and seven of eight items validated above the operational threshold, particular regarding the framework's coherence, completeness and originality. Expert feedback also informed ten contextual refinements addressing financial sustainability, institutional continuity, and governance coordination. The proposed Framework aims to support decision-makers in planning, implementing, and sustaining digital initiatives in alignment with institutional realities and stakeholder expectations.

title: Analyzing FinTech and sustainable development through the triple bottom line framework using bibliometric analysis
summary: The present study explores the intellectual structure and thematic evolution of FinTech-enabled sustainable development through the Triple Bottom Line (TBL) framework. The paper highlights the use of FinTech innovations to advance sustainable development while balancing the economic (Profit), social (People), and environmental (Planet) dimensions. A bibliometric study was conducted using publications in the Scopus database. Bibliometric analysis, including publication trends, influential journals, leading authors, countries and institutions, co-authorship analysis, keyword co-occurrence analysis, and thematic mapping, was employed using Biblioshiny and VoSviewer to identify emerging directions in the field. This paper examined 3375 records extracted from the Scopus database on 28th January 2026, related to FinTech and to economic, social, and environmental sustainability between 2015 and 2026. The findings show a decent growth in FinTech and sustainable development research, with China emerging as the most influential country in the field for substantive study. The TBL-based classification reveals a concentration of study within the ‘People’ and ‘Profit’ dimensions, whereas the ‘Planet’ dimension remains relatively understudied. The field is rapidly evolving, with an average article age of approximately 2.69 years, reflecting the recent and growing scholarly interest in FinTech-enabled sustainable development. The study integrates FinTech literature with the TBL framework through a bibliometric analysis. It extends previous studies by systematically categorizing research themes across ‘People-Planet-Profit’ dimensions. The findings suggest theoretical, practical, and policy implications for promoting sustainability in the FinTech ecosystem by placing greater emphasis on green finance, climate-focused innovation, and inclusive digital financial services.

title: ESG pillars, firm value, and economic volatility in U.S. healthcare firms
summary: Abstract This study examines how environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance and economic volatility relate to firm value and operating performance in U.S. healthcare firms. Using firm and year fixed effects, we find that the annual change in the social pillar, rather than the composite score or the environmental and governance pillars, is positively associated with market value, consistent with social issues being financially material in healthcare. The estimate is imprecise when the sample is restricted to 2015 through 2024, and within the sector the association is not found among providers and services. ESG shows no contemporaneous accounting reward and a small negative association with return on assets, and economic volatility is not robustly related to firm value, although regional volatility is positively associated with return on assets. Overall, we provide associational evidence that materiality informed, pillar level analysis is more informative than aggregate ESG scores.

title: Teaching Risk Management and Control in Accounting Higher Education: A Judgment-Centered Pedagogical Framework
summary: Risk management and control are central to accounting practice, yet their treatment in higher education is often fragmented across auditing, management accounting, information systems, and corporate governance courses. Teaching can consequently privilege framework recall and procedural compliance over the judgment required to interpret uncertainty, challenge assumptions, and communicate responses. This conceptual paper examines how accounting-related degree programs can integrate risk management and control through coherent teaching methods and curriculum modes. Drawing on a structured synthesis of accounting education, risk and control, and professional learning literature, the paper defines judgment-centered risk capability as the capacity to frame objectives and context, diagnose vulnerabilities, deliberate over alternative responses, communicate accountable decisions, and learn from subsequent experience. It proposes an aligned pedagogical framework combining progressive case-based inquiry, interrupted scenario simulations, role rotation, dialogic debriefing, and workplace-connected learning. These methods are supported by authentic assessment through risk-framing memoranda, control rationales, decision logs, oral defenses, and reflective portfolios. Implementation is organized as a spiral curriculum in which foundational concepts are revisited across accounting domains with increasing ambiguity and stakeholder complexity. Particular attention is given to faculty collaboration, proportionate use of digital environments, inclusion, academic integrity, and assurance of learning. The paper contributes a pedagogical connection between risk frameworks and professional formation rather than another classification of teaching techniques. It offers universities design principles for developing graduates who understand that controls are organizational choices with behavioral and ethical consequences. The framework is conceptual and does not claim demonstrated causal effectiveness; future research should investigate its operation across institutional and professional contexts.

title: A hybrid data prioritization and neural network framework for cost‑optimized supply chain management
summary: The increasing complexity and volatility of modern supply chains necessitate intelligent decision-support systems that can efficiently process vast amounts of operational data while maintaining computational tractability. Traditional supply chain optimization models often fail to leverage the inherent structure of operational data, leading to suboptimal resource allocation and increased costs. Existing approaches in supply chain management (SCM) typically treat forecasting and optimization as separate stages, with data preprocessing methods, including computational sorting, serving merely as preliminary steps without any formal integration into the decision-making framework. This separation results in missed opportunities for improving operational efficiency and responsiveness. This study proposes a novel hybrid framework that formally integrates a data prioritization mechanism inspired by computational sorting principles with a neural network (NN)-based forecasting model within a unified cost-minimization mathematical programming framework. The prioritization mechanism generates a composite priority score (δij) derived from demand, cost, and inventory attributes, which is then embedded as an upper bound on assignment variables in the optimization model to guide resource allocation decisions. The framework is validated through comprehensive numerical experiments across 10 diverse supply chain scenarios, with each instance replicated 30 times to ensure statistical reliability. The primary scientific contribution lies in the mathematical formalization of the data prioritization process and its integration as operational constraints in the optimization model, rather than treating sorting as a mere preprocessing step. This formal linkage between data characteristics and optimization decisions distinguishes our approach from prior studies. Computational results, validated through Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) with F = 28.4 and p < 0.001, demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves superior performance. The Hybrid Framework reduces Mean Absolute Error (MAE) by 40.7% (from 178.50 to 105.80) compared to Single Sorting methods, and achieves a 12.1% reduction in average total cost compared to Data Science methods (from 14,528 to 12,769) and a 22.2% reduction compared to Single Sorting methods (from 16,407 to 12,769). The framework delivers a service level of 94.2%, significantly higher than the 86.6% achieved by Single Sorting and 89.6% by Data Science methods. Sensitivity analysis confirms robustness, maintaining service levels above 90% even under high demand variability (CV = 0.8), while scalability analysis demonstrates near-linear growth in computation time, with large-scale instances (50 × 20) solved in approximately 15 min (920 s). These findings underscore the practical potential of the proposed approach as a robust decision-support tool for strategic and tactical supply chain planning, offering managers a data-driven pathway to improve operational resilience and efficiency. title: Consumer Low-Carbon Preferences on Supply Chain Decision-Making and Coordination Mechanisms
summary: Customers' predilection for sustainable items is steadily promoting supply chains to undergo low-carbon transformation, making consumer low-carbon preferences a significant demand-side factor influencing supply chain decision-making mechanisms. This article focuses on consumers' low-carbon preferences, systematically sorting out their role logic in supply chain pricing, emission reduction production, and green marketing decisions, further exploring the internal causes of coordination difficulties across supply networks in decentralized decision contexts, and distinguishing the applicable boundaries and implementation effects of different coordination mechanisms. Research has found that consumers' low-carbon preferences do not necessarily lead to synchronous improvements in supply chain emissions reduction and economic benefits. Contract parameters and corporate behavioral preferences can regulate the transmission effect of demand signals. Under the coordination mechanism of cost sharing, benefit sharing, and incorporating behavioral preferences, low-carbon consumption demand can only be transformed into overall supply chain performance when specific boundary conditions are matched. This article clarifies the constraints on the transformation of low-carbon preferences into supply chain performance, which can provide a literature basis for modeling and empirical studies concerning low-carbon supply networks.

title: Rethinking resilience: bridging due diligence gaps to mitigate supply chain risks
summary: Purpose The purpose of this study is to examine the key factors affecting supply chain due diligence (SCDD), evaluating their associated risks and proposing appropriate mitigation strategies that bridge due diligence gaps and strengthen resilience in global supply chains. Design/methodology/approach Key due diligence factors were identified through a comprehensive literature review and expert consultations. The study adopts a multimethod approach that integrates multiple theoretical perspectives, the Fuzzy Evidential Reasoning Algorithm (FERA) and risk profiling analysis. Findings The results identify critical due diligence factors, including regulatory compliance, transparency, supplier evaluation, ethical sourcing, data governance and sustainability practices, that significantly influence governance, operational stability and environmental performance. The study further develops targeted mitigation strategies based on risk intensity and strategic priority. Practical implications The proposed framework supports practitioners and policymakers in making risk-sensitive decisions to strengthen due diligence, improve transparency, enhance compliance and build more resilient and sustainable supply chain operations. Originality/value This study contributes to the SCDD literature by integrating governance, operational and sustainability dimensions within a unified prioritization framework, building on the established FERA rather than proposing a new computational technique. The framework offers a systematic approach for identifying and mitigating due diligence gaps in global supply chains, with SDGs 8, 9 and 13 addressed as an indicative conceptual mapping rather than a directly measured outcome.

title: ETDP: a high-performance transportation delay prediction framework with explanations for supply chains
summary: Purpose This work aims to develop a transportation delay prediction framework to improve prediction performance while providing explanations for its predictions. Design/methodology/approach An ETDP (high-performance Transportation Delay Prediction Framework with Explanations) for supply chains is proposed, in which we design an LGFT (Local-Global Fusion Transformer) model for high-performance prediction, and integrate LGFT with SHAP to explain its predictions. LGFT captures local feature interaction patterns via 1D CNN and global nonlinear relationships via an MLP, which are then fused through a Transformer Encoder to model long-range contextual dependencies. Integrated with SHAP, ETDP formalizes a three-level explanation mechanism that can analyze global feature importance, key feature dependency, and instance-level attribution. Findings The ETDP framework is evaluated on three public supply chain datasets covering binary delay prediction, last-mile logistics, and five-class supply chain risk classification. On DataCo, ETDP achieves the highest precision and remains competitive across the other evaluation indicators. On India, it obtains the best recall, F1-score, and MCC in the held-out test evaluation. On Mendeley, it reaches the best accuracy, recall, MCC, and lowest FNR, while remaining descriptively close to XGBoost in F1-score, though below it in precision and probability-ranking metrics. Repeated-run analyses show statistically supported improvements over several representative baselines, although ETDP does not uniformly dominate every model and metric. Originality/value ETDP is a useful combination of predictive modeling and post hoc explainability for transportation delay prediction. Fusing local and global features, it contributes a high-performance prediction model. Integrating with SHAP, it provides a supply-chain-oriented three-level explanation workflow. It can support both early delay-risk sensing and more targeted intervention prioritization, such as strategic optimization, context-specific risk mitigation and specific order diagnostics. title: Green fiscal policy and green finance in mitigating environmental deterioration in Central European regions
summary: Environmental deterioration has intensified across Central Europe as rapid economic expansion continues to rely heavily on resource extraction, fossil fuel consumption, and industrial emissions. This growing ecological pressure has renewed interest in policy instruments capable of steering regions toward sustainable development. Motivated by these concerns, this investigation assessed how green fiscal policy (GFP), green finance (GRF), patent applications (PAP), renewable energy (REN), and natural resource rent (NAR) influence carbon emissions (CAR) in 13 Central European economies with data from 1990–2022. The analysis applies a series of diagnostics followed by the Cross Sectionally Augmented Autoregressive Distributed Lag (CS ARDL) model, supported by FMOLS robustness and Dumitrescu–Hurlin causality tests. The results reveal that GFP, GRF, and REN significantly reduce carbon emissions in both the short and long run. Conversely, NAR and PAP unexpectedly appreciate emissions, depicting inefficiencies in resource governance and the limited environmental orientation of current innovation activities. The D&H causality illustrated both unidirectional and bidirectional causality among the variables. These findings imply that Central European economies can accelerate their transition toward ecological sustainability by strengthening carbon pricing mechanisms, renewable energy investment, restructuring green finance portfolios to low carbon technologies, and enforcing sustainable resource extraction practices for long term carbon neutrality.

title: Pengaruh Penerapan Green Accounting, Kinerja Lingkungan dan Intellectual Capital Terhadap Kinerja Keuangan Dengan Good Corporate Governance Sebagai Variabel Moderasi Pada Perusahaan Perkebunan Kelapa Sawit

summary: In just a few decades Majid Al Futtaim (“the Group”) had established an empire boasting major shopping malls, successful retail chains and popular entertainment centres across the Middle East, Asia, and North Africa (MENA) region. By 2020, however, its competitive landscape was changing fast, with diverse players striving to define the future of retail. Traditional powerhouses such as Walmart, with their extensive physical presences, and tech titans such as Amazon, rich with consumer data and technological prowess, were changing the way consumers shopped and interacted with brands. Whose business model would triumph in the dynamic environment of the Middle East? And how should traditional companies such as Majid Al Futtaim respond to the new landscape?

title: Legal Aspects of Fintech in India
summary: Fintech has widened the access to payments, credit and investment in India, but its characteristics of speed and anonymity have also enabled rising financial fraud and unauthorized advice. This paper asks whether India's legal framework is equipped enough to adequately protect the consumers on digital financial platforms. Rather than treating Fintech as a single category, it analyses two regulators: the Reserve Bank of India, which governs payments and digital lending, and the Securities and Exchange Board of India, which governs robo-advisory, algorithmic trading and unregistered "finfluencers". Using a doctrinal methodology of research, it examines statutes, directions, regulations and circulars, alongside fraud data and the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023. It finds that regulation has followed market development rather than anticipating them, that several activities fit poorly within existing regulatory categories, and that regulation alone, without enforcement, cannot curb fraud without enforcement, awareness and coordination. The most significant gaps between regimes, including fragmented grievance redressal and overlapping breach-reporting duties. The paper recommends closer inter-regulatory coordination and a dedicated robo-advisory framework, proportionate influencer registration and clearer alignment with the DPDP Act.

title: Corporate Storytelling through CSR Disclosures During and After COVID-19: Evidence from Indian Pharmaceutical Firms
summary: The COVID-19 pandemic changed the priorities of corporate social responsibility (CSR) and communication practices, especially in the pharmaceutical industry. This paper explores the ways in which major Indian pharmaceutical firms used CSR disclosures as strategic narrative in the midst of the pandemic and after it. CSR parts of Annual Reports, Business Responsibility and Sustainability Reports (BRSR), and other disclosures of eleven companies (2020-2023) were content analysed, using thematic analysis, sentiment analysis, and word frequency, with the help of a mixed-method content analysis. Findings show that there is a distinct shift in the narrative of pandemic relief and healthcare support to sustainability, ESG integration, digital health, and long-term development programs in the post-pandemic era. Mostly positive sentiment indicates the attempts to preserve legitimacy and confidence of stakeholders. The results underscore CSR reporting as a strategic communication tool that is not necessarily related to regulatory compliance.

title: Integration of Construction Supply Chain Management and Project Controls for Improved Cost Performance in Mega Projects
summary: Cost escalation in megaprojects is frequently recorded as a project-controls problem although a material proportion of its antecedents originates outside the conventional cost ledger: in supplier capacity, procurement decisions, fabrication readiness, delivery uncertainty and poorly sequenced site work. This integrative review examines how construction supply chain management (CSCM) can be connected to project controls to improve the timeliness and reliability of cost decisions. Thirty DOI-identifiable publications dated 2020–2025 provide the core analytical literature, complemented by critical examination of the managerial mechanisms linking procurement and production information to schedule and cost forecasts. The review adopts thematic synthesis rather than a statistical meta-analysis because the publications differ in design, context and outcome measures. Four interdependent mechanisms emerge: a common work-package data structure; supplier-informed lookahead and change control; reconciliation of earned value, commitments and remaining exposure; and governance that assigns accountability for corrective action. An integrated control architecture and an explicitly hypothetical, internally reconciled numerical example illustrate how cost signals can change when upstream commitments and schedule consequences become visible. The argument is not that technology independently creates savings, but that decision quality improves when trusted supply-chain evidence is translated into actionable project forecasts. The paper develops research propositions and a validation agenda for complex, multi-contractor delivery environments, while identifying contractual, data-quality and organizational conditions under which integration may fail.

title: The more confident the more digital? A study of the mechanisms of CEO overconfidence on corporate digital transformation
summary: Purpose This study examines how CEO overconfidence influences corporate digital transformation and explores the cognitive-behavioral mechanisms underlying this relationship. Design/methodology/approach Using a panel dataset of Chinese A-share listed firms from 2010 to 2024, this study constructs a language-based measure of CEO overconfidence from CEOs' personal social media posts and their directly attributable statements reported in publicly available sources. Two-way fixed-effects models are employed to examine the relationship between CEO overconfidence and corporate digital transformation, supplemented by robustness checks including alternative measures, additional fixed effects, instrumental variable analyses and Heckman two-stage analysis. Findings The results show that CEO overconfidence is positively associated with firms' digital transformation. This effect operates primarily through entrepreneurial orientation and strategic risk-taking, with the two mechanisms forming a sequential mediating relationship. Furthermore, the positive effect of CEO overconfidence on digital transformation is strengthened when CEOs possess an IT background and greater CEO power, as well as when firms have higher levels of resource slack and operate in regions with higher levels of market development, but is weakened in state-owned enterprises. Originality/value This study advances upper echelons theory by developing a commitment-based account of how CEO overconfidence shapes strategic change under uncertainty and by specifying a cognition–posture–action process through which executive cognition is translated into firm-level digital transformation. Methodologically, it introduces a language-based measure of CEO overconfidence derived from CEOs' linguistic expressions, offering an alternative approach to capturing executive cognition beyond traditional financial proxies.

title: ACHIEVING PERFORMANCE IMPROVEMENT IN THE ERA OF SUPPLY CHAIN DIGITALIZATION: EMPIRICAL STUDY FROM THE JORDANIAN HEALTH SECTOR
summary: This research aims to study the relationship between Supply Chain Digitalization and the organizational performance within the Jordanian healthcare sector, where the mediating role of Supply Chain integration and the moderating role of Technological turbulence will be discussed. The study adopted descriptive analytical research, which is a quantitative type of research. A stratified random sampling method was implemented to determine 200 employees from the public and private hospitals within Jordan to be included in the sample. In order to investigate the study variables, a structured questionnaire was used; the scales in the questionnaires were already validated. To investigate the hypothesized direct, mediating, and moderating relationships, structural equation modeling (SEM) was then performed with the software program called SmartPLS. Results indicated that the effect of supply chain digitalization on supply chain integration is significant, while the effect is also significant on organizational performance. Moreover, the relationship between supply chain digitalization and organizational performance was partially mediated by supply chain integration, indicating that supply chain digitalization has a direct relationship with organizational performance as well as through supply chain integration. The results also revealed a significant moderating role of technological turbulence, where a higher level of technological turbulence enhanced the relationships among supply chain digitalization, supply chain integration, and organizational performance. The results highlighted the relevance of SC-D and SC-I to improve the organizational performance, especially in Technologically-Dynamic Environments. The study adds to the literature in terms of presenting empirical evidence about the relationship between supply chain digitalization, supply chain integration, and technological turbulence and organizational performance in the healthcare industry. In practice, the findings should inform the hospital administration and policymakers on the significance of digital capability development and supply chain integration to increase hospital performance when facing technological turbulence of different degrees.

title: Abnormal Production Activity in an Emerging Market: Short-Term Accounting Gains, Inventory Accumulation, and Cash-Flow Consequences
summary: This study examines the economic consequences of abnormal production activity among Vietnamese listed manufacturing firms by investigating its effects on accounting performance, inventory accumulation, and future operating cash flows. Using an unbalanced panel of 243 firms over the period 2016–2024, abnormal production activity is estimated using the normal production cost model [2], and the hypotheses are tested with firm fixed-effects regressions. The results show that abnormal production activity improves short-term accounting performance but does not enhance longer-term performance, operating cash flows, or market-based performance. It also increases subsequent inventory intensity, while firms with high inventory intensity experience weaker future operating cash flows. These findings suggest that the accounting benefits of abnormal production activity are temporary and accompanied by inventory-related operating costs, providing new evidence on the economic consequences of production-based real earnings management in an emerging market.

title: Digital Economy Policy Exposure and Firms' Innovation in Key Core Technologies
summary: Digital policy can influence strategic innovation through policy exposure, complementary organizational investment, and lengthy technology-conversion cycles. This study examines whether intelligent manufacturing policy is associated with firms' innovation in key core technologies among Chinese listed companies. Policy exposure is defined by whether an industry was prioritized by the policy and whether the observation falls in the post-policy period. A difference-in-differences framework with firm and year fixed effects is used to estimate relative changes in patent outcomes. The results show a positive post-policy association for granted key core technology patents, including alternative outcome measures based on transformed grants and patent citations. The financing-constraint result does not support a financing-relief mechanism, whereas the decline in industry concentration is consistent with a more competitive market structure. The technical-personnel share does not change significantly. Estimated associations are stronger among firms with greater digital-technology use and higher robot penetration. However, the event-study evidence does not adequately support parallel trends. The findings should therefore be interpreted as conditional associations rather than definitive causal effects.

title: Improved European native seed supply chains are essential for the implementation of the Nature Restoration Regulation
summary: Abstract To support the implementation of the EU Nature Restoration Regulation (NRR), there is an unprecedented need to scale up ecosystem restoration, which requires radical improvements to the European seed supply chain, especially for herbaceous species. The fundamental tradeoff between the need for local provenance and climate resilience, as well as practical constraints on seed availability, generates a bottleneck for restoration practice and may jeopardize the implementation of the NRR. Here, we overview the current legislative context for plant reproductive material, assess the status of native seed supply, and propose institutional and operational solutions to strengthen seed supply chains in Europe. We call for the adoption of the concept of Native Seed and Restoration Centres (NSRCs) to boost seed supply chains. We outline the main functions and responsibilities of NSRCs, and highlight the short‐ to mid‐term actions that are crucial for enhancing the availability and use of native seeds.

title: Sustainability in halal food supply chains: A systematic review from an Islamic ethical perspective
summary: This study synthesises and reconceptualises sustainability in halal food supply chains by positioning Islamic ethical principles as a governance-oriented ethical order rather than as a procedural extension of conventional sustainability frameworks. A systematic literature review was conducted using the Scopus database without publication year restrictions. The initial search yielded 396 publications, of which 63 peer-reviewed articles were retained following title, abstract, and full-text screening and analysed through thematic synthesis. The findings indicate that sustainability in halal food supply chain research is conceptualised in fragmented and inconsistent ways, most commonly through certification, traceability, and assurance mechanisms. Although economic, social, and environmental dimensions are widely addressed, Islamic ethical principles are generally embedded implicitly within compliance structures rather than articulated as explicit organising logics. As a result, sustainability is operationalised primarily through technical and procedural mechanisms, with limited attention to ethical coordination, accountability, and responsibility across supply chain actors. The analysis reconceptualises Islamic sustainability as a value-based ethical order grounded in moral obligation, stewardship, and accountability that governs intention, process, and coordination across halal food supply chains. This perspective clarifies the distinctiveness of Islamic sustainability from conventional sustainability approaches and highlights the need to move beyond compliance-oriented practices towards ethics-based sustainability governance. The study contributes to halal supply chain scholarship by providing a clearer conceptual foundation for understanding sustainability from an Islamic perspective.

title: Application of Internet of Things (IoT) on Improving Performance within Global Manufacturing Supply Chains
summary: Internet of Things (IoT) in the context of supply chains (SC) is mainly observed with integration to build resilience. It has discussed the rationale in terms of disruptions caused by the pandemic, the economic and political situation. It has elaborated on the issues such as labor and material shortages affecting demand and supply sides. IoT impacts greatly on the manufacturing SC to enhance efficiency and transparency. Besides this, the implementation of IoT technology has monitored manufacturing procedures and enhanced productivity to deliver a safer working space. In addition to this, this technology has improved supply chain performance to resolve the operational bottleneck and use OTA methods. The study has discussed the factors related to the vulnerabilities of IoT systems, and it has mainly focused on security issues leading to increased concerns. In the context of a SC system, organization and supplier networks are required to work together to get optimal performance. The study explores different methodologies for collecting data. Interpretivism philosophy, exploratory design, inductive approach, and secondary data collection methods have been chosen in this study. Data has been provided in support of the findings in linking them with objectives. It includes that IoT can use different techniques to improve the SC performance and advance the production process.

title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption and Supply Chain Finance: Evidence from China's A-Share Listed Firms
summary: In recent years companies have used artificial intelligence (AI) to raise efficiency, to support decisions and to process data. This paper uses Chinese A-share listed companies to test whether firm-level AI adoption helps supply chain finance to grow. The AI index comes from text analysis of annual reports, and a panel over 2011 to 2023 is estimated; AI adoption is positively related to supply chain finance, and its coefficient stays stable after the model controls firm size, leverage, profitability and market value. The data come from the CSMAR database and annual reports; the sample drops financial and special treatment (ST) firms, keeps firm-years with more than 300 employees, and adds firm and year fixed effects to absorb unobserved firm features and macro shocks. The subsample results show that the positive relation is mainly in medium and large firms; there AI raises financing demand, information transparency and credit access, and this supports supply chain finance. Formal coefficient-difference tests show that this relation is significantly weaker in relatively small firms, and medium-sized and large firms show no statistical difference.

title: Digital transformation in healthcare: a systematic and bibliometric review of strategies, policies, barriers, and benefits
summary: Digital transformation (DT) in healthcare has traditionally been conceptualized through models that privilege either technological or organizational perspectives. However, this study shows that DT cannot be understood as a linear or purely technical process but rather as a dynamic adjustment among policy frameworks, organizational capabilities, and technological change. To capture this complexity, we conducted a systematic and integrative review that combined bibliometric mapping and a grounded qualitative synthesis of literature published between 2010 and 2025, guided by three research questions: (RQ1) What are the key themes and trends in healthcare DT? (RQ2) What policy-level barriers and enablers shape its development? and (RQ3) What strategic challenges and benefits influence DT in healthcare institutions? Findings reveal that prevailing models—such as the HIMSS EMRAM and McKinsey 7S frameworks—offer valuable benchmarks but remain limited by static and technocentric assumptions. Building on these insights, this study proposes an integrated framework grounded in Social Systems Theory, which conceptualizes DT as an adaptive system characterized by iterative feedback, learning, and recalibration across policy, organizational, and technological domains. The framework contributes both a theoretical advancement toward an evolutionary understanding of DT and a practical roadmap for policymakers and healthcare managers aiming to build sustainable, interoperable, and human-centered health systems.

title: Design and validation of a measurement scale for digital transformation capabilities in agricultural settings
summary: Digital transformation is essential for strengthening agri-food systems in emerging economies. However, there is a lack of validated tools to assess both the capabilities and levels of digital maturity in agricultural production units. This research validates an instrument to measure Digital Transformation (DT) capabilities and levels of digital maturity in agricultural production units (APU) in an emerging economy. The instrument encompasses six dimensions: sensing, seizing and transforming capabilities, along with the stages of digital maturity, digitization, digitalization, and digital transformation. The validation process was developed in five stages, including theoretical foundation, item development, expert review, and exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses, applied to a sample of 68 potato farmers from south-central Chile. The final instrument consists of 32 items with promising psychometric properties; reliability and validity indicators met recommended thresholds across most dimensions, with a small number of exceptions discussed in the study. The results reveal that farmers widely recognize the value of digital technology and demonstrate a willingness to invest, despite being in early stages of digitalization, with widespread use of basic tools such as smartphones and messaging applications, but with limited adoption of more advanced technologies such as precision agriculture. This gap between perceived value and actual implementation highlights the role of structural barriers in rural contexts. This instrument offers researchers and policymakers a promising, albeit preliminary, tool to assess dynamic capabilities and digital maturity at the individual farmer level, representing an initial step toward diagnostic tools for digital transformation processes in this context.

title: The National Information-for-Citizens-Benefit Pilot Policy and Corporate Digital Transformation
summary: Using the implementation of the national Information-for-Citizens-Benefit pilot, this paper matches the registered location of enterprises with the annual reports and financial data of A-share listed companies on the Shanghai and Shenzhen markets from 2008 to 2024, and uses the difference-in-differences method to examine whether government information integration changes corporate digital behavior. The estimation results show that after entering the pilot, the digital word frequency in corporate annual reports increases significantly. Further analysis finds that bank loan balances rise, the internal control index improves, and the incidence of internal control failure declines. The policy effect is stronger in enterprises with higher ex-ante financing constraints; the within-group effect is significant in cities with better digital foundations, but the between-group difference across cities is not yet significant. The above evidence indicates that government information integration and government process adjustment can influence corporate digital choices, and can be explained from two aspects: external financing and internal governance.

title: Digital Transformation of the Financial Model of a Global Technology Corporation: The Case of Microsoft
summary: The article is devoted to the analysis of the digital transformation of Microsoft's financial model under the company shifting from a licence- and product-centred logic towards a cloud-platform and AI-oriented architecture. The purpose of the study is to identify the mechanisms, through which cloud services, subscription monetisation, ecosystem integration, and artificial intelligence reshape the company’s revenue structure, operating leverage, capital intensity, and cash flows. The methodological basis is formed of the case method, systemic and comparative analysis, content analysis of corporate reporting and dynamic analysis of indicators for the fiscal years 2024–2026. It is established that revenue and operating income growth is accompanied by a sharp increase in capital inclusion of data processing and computing infrastructure. The research substantiates that the financial effect of Microsoft's digital transformation is awash with duplicity: recurring revenues and AI monetisation strengthen revenue resilience, while they increase capital intensity of the model. The practical significance of the research results may be used to assess digital strategies of large technology companies.
